apsDecisions.title: Enhanced coherence of rare-earth nuclear spins in a crystal

detailFetch.abstract: Rare-earth ions in crystals are useful in precision measurements and quantum information science because of their exceptional optical and spin coherence properties. We show that the nuclear spin coherence time of 153 E u 3 + ions doped into yttrium orthosilicate can be significantly enhanced by driving the environmental nuclear spins in the host crystal. This method of enhancing the spin coherence time can lead to improved precision measurements using rare-earth-doped crystals.

apsDecisions.selectionReason: Eu³⁺:Y₂SiO₅核自旋相干增强，固态自旋相关但未涉及本期生长或关联电子主线。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Rare-earth ions in crystals are useful in precision measurements and quantum information science because of their exceptional optical and spin coherence properties. We show that the nuclear spin coherence time of 153Eu3+ ions doped into yttrium orthosilicate can be significantly enhanced by driving the environmental nuclear spins in the host crystal. This method of enhancing the spin coherence time can lead to improved precision measurements using rare-earth-doped crystals.

apsDecisions.title: Multipartite Bell-Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger nonclassicality from interwoven frustrated down-conversion
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We present a theory of an interference process that starts with N coherently pumped two-mode parametric down-conversion (PDC) sources, whose output modes are directed to N observers such that each observer receives modes from two different source crystals. Each observation station is equipped with a locally controlled PDC crystal, coherently pumped with the source crystals, whose output modes are perfectly aligned with the input modes from the source PDCs. By varying the local phases of the input modes, perfect 2N-photon interference is observed in 2N single-photon registrations, one in each output mode of the local PDCs. The interference results from the indistinguishability of the origins of the detected photons: either they all originate from the source PDCs or from the local PDCs. Bell-Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger nonclassicality of the process emerges when one considers situations in which at least one of the local PDC processes is blocked and the 2N-photon interference disappears. A “lifted” Clauser-Horne inequality is violated when its sole negative correlation term is tuned to maximal destructive interference, while all other terms involve settings in which one of the local pumps is off.

apsDecisions.title: Spectral theory of energy-selective quantum search with Ising Hamiltonian phase oracles
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We develop an exact spectral-response theory for the Grover-type iterate WT=Dξexp(−iTH), in which the evolution generated by a diagonal Ising Hamiltonian is used directly as a continuous phase oracle. An energy-grouped recurrence and its generating-function solution show how the empirical characteristic function determines the position, width, height, and saturation time of an energy-selective resonance. For an annealed Gaussian density of states, a high-density-tail resonance containing M configurations is reached after Θ(2n/M) oracle calls with success probability Θ(1), giving a quadratic query improvement over independent uniform sampling with classical energy evaluation. For correlated random Ising spectra, overlap-dependent covariances lead to a realization-dependent resonance shift with root-mean-square scale O(n−3), parametrically larger than the resonance width, and can also reduce the peak height. The shift is both an algorithmic detuning and a coherent probe of sample-specific spectral fluctuations whose ensemble statistics reflect the Ising overlap structure. Spectral symmetrization and iterative calibration can remove or compensate the resonance-center displacement for prescribed-energy targeting. We also clarify the relation to designed spectral filters and the precision and coherence requirements of this asymptotic primitive.

apsDecisions.title: Lower bounding the secret key capacity of bosonic Gaussian channels via optimal Gaussian measurements
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We find the maximum rate achievable in the private communication over a bosonic quantum channel with a fully Gaussian protocol based on optimal single-mode Gaussian measurements. This rate establishes a lower bound on the secret rate capacity of the channel. We focus on the class of phase-insensitive Gaussian channels. For the thermal loss and thermal amplification channels, our results demonstrate the optimality, within the constraints of our analysis, of previously proposed protocols, while also providing a significantly simplified formula for their performance evaluation. For the added noise channel, our rate provides a better lower bound than any previously known.

apsDecisions.title: Light-induced line narrowing of the magnetic resonance in a parametric resonance optically pumped rubidium magnetometer
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Optically pumped atomic magnetometers are fundamentally limited by spin-exchange relaxation in finite magnetic fields. In conventional parametric resonance magnetometers (PRMs), this relaxation dominates the resonance linewidth, producing broad profiles that degrade sensitivity. Here, we suppress this relaxation by incorporating light narrowing via optical pumping into spin-stretched states in a longitudinally modulated PRM, which directly enables dual-axis vector detection of transverse magnetic fields through lock-in demodulation. Under optimized conditions, the magnetometer achieves transverse sensitivities of 210fT/Hz and 290fT/Hz along two orthogonal axes, a 3-dB bandwidth of about 500Hz, and excellent cross-axis discrimination—an order-of-magnitude improvement over conventional PRMs. This work demonstrates that light narrowing effectively overcomes the spin-exchange limitation in finite-field operation, providing a promising route for high-sensitivity vector magnetometry in applications such as atomic gyroscopes and active magnetic compensation.

apsDecisions.title: Charging efficiency bursts in a quantum battery with cyclic indefinite causal order
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Enhancement of quantum battery performance is a popular subject in quantum thermodynamics. An interesting phenomenon is the quick charging effect [Phys. Rev. Res. 6, 023136 (2024)], which has been explored by utilizing a quantum interferometric technique known as superposition of trajectories. A similar technique used to boost quantum battery performance is indefinite causal order. Here, we propose a charging protocol that utilizes cyclic indefinite causal order, whereby N charging sequences are superposed when utilizing N chargers. We observe charging efficiency bursts when implementing our cyclic indefinite charging protocol. The duration of these bursts increases with N. Additionally, we present a circuit model to implement our charging protocol for the two-charger scenario and perform proof-of-concept demonstrations on IonQ, Quantinuum, and IBMQ quantum processors. The results validate the existence of charging efficiency bursts as shown by our theoretical analysis and numerical simulations.

apsDecisions.title: Topological defect states via local symmetry breaking in modified Haldane models
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Antichiral edge states extend the conventional bulk-edge correspondence by allowing edge modes on two parallel boundaries to propagate in the same direction, compensated by counterpropagating bulk states. However, their strong localization at physical boundaries leads to a severe dependence on boundary conditions and a lack of effective radiation suppression, hindering their practical application in optical communications. Here we propose a control mechanism based on local symmetry breaking in a modified Haldane photonic crystal. By tuning the geometric parameters of boundary rods, antichiral edge states can be merged into and hybridized with the projected bulk continuum. By reversing this mechanism, we create internal line defects that induce coupled interface modes inside the crystal. These modes form topological defect states that retain the unidirectional transport and topological origin of the antichiral system, while exhibiting quality factors several orders of magnitude higher than those of edge states. We experimentally demonstrate a defect waveguide and defect cavity and observe selective coupling from traveling waves to discrete circulating resonant modes. The resonant frequency can be tuned by geometric modulation. This work provides a low-loss and internally integrated route for constructing nonreciprocal topological photonic devices.

apsDecisions.title: Ultrafast electron-impact-excited N 2 superfluorescence in femtosecond filaments
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We demonstrate that the 337-nm emission from neutral nitrogen molecules, pumped via incoherent electron-impact excitation in circularly polarized femtosecond filaments, is oscillatory superfluorescence (SF) rather than amplified spontaneous emission. Time-resolved measurements reveal that both the pulse duration and the emission delay scale as P−1/2 with nitrogen pressure, providing a definitive signature of gain-swept SF. These dynamics are quantitatively reproduced by bidirectional Maxwell-Bloch simulations that incorporate impulsive electron-impact excitation and fine-structure quantum beats. Our results demonstrate that macroscopic quantum coherence emerges following ultrafast electron-impact pumping and persists in atmospheric-pressure plasmas despite rapid collisional dephasing. These results establish femtosecond filaments as a robust platform for studying collective molecular phenomena and provide a framework for generating remote, coherent UV sources in the atmosphere.

apsDecisions.title: Simultaneous ground-state cooling of six mechanical modes of two levitated nanoparticles
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Ground-state cooling is a prerequisite for exploring macroscopic quantum effects in mechanical motion of massive objects. Here, we construct a polarization-angle-controllable coupled cavity-levitated-nanoparticle system in which two nanoparticles trapped by individual tweezers are coupled to a single-mode field in a cavity. We also study the simultaneous ground-state cooling of six mechanical displacement modes of the two levitated nanoparticles through the coherent scattering mechanism. By deriving the Hamiltonian of the system and performing the linearization, we obtain a linearized seven-mode Hamiltonian which can exhibit the coupling structure and cooling mechanism. We confirm the physical condition for the appearance of dark modes, which will suppress the simultaneous ground-state cooling of these mechanical modes. We also find that by properly tuning the polarization angle θ between the cavity field and the optical tweezer fields, the coupling channels can be controlled on demand and simultaneous ground-state cooling of these six motional modes of the two nanoparticles can be realized. Our work paves the way for generation and manipulation of collective macroscopic quantum effects in multiple levitated nanoparticles.

apsDecisions.title: Regular and chaotic dynamics of nonlinear optomechanical systems controlled by modulated light
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: The nonlinear dynamics of a mechanical resonator in an optomechanical system with linear, quadratic, and cubic photon-vibration interactions (with respect to mechanical displacements) in a modulated driving field under conditions of adiabatic elimination of the optical field is studied. Based on the constructed bifurcation diagrams of the mechanical coordinate and the largest Lyapunov exponent as a function of the modulation amplitude, as well as power spectra, phase portraits, and Poincaré sections, regions of regular and chaotic dynamics of the optomechanical system are identified. It is also shown that for a certain modulation amplitude in the presence of all three types of interactions, chaotic dynamics of the mechanical resonator (oscillator) is realized, which is replaced by quasiperiodic oscillations in the absence of cubic interaction, and the system returns to chaotic behavior only if linear interaction remains. This nonmonotonic dependence of chaotic dynamics on the order of nonlinearity originates from the interplay between parametric driving and effective potential reshaping and manifests that nonlinearity does not always enhance chaos. For an optomechanical system in a membrane-in-the-middle configuration, where only quadratic photon-vibration interaction is present, it is demonstrated that at small modulation amplitudes the mechanical oscillator exhibits quasiperiodic motion in each of the wells of a symmetric two-minimum potential, whereas large modulation amplitudes lead to chaotic motion, involving interwell transitions.

apsDecisions.title: Synergistic charging of a quantum battery via Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction and non-Markovian noise
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Protecting quantum batteries from environmental noise remains a challenge. Using exact Burshtein-Kubo equations, we study a two-spin quantum battery with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) coupling under independent local longitudinal random telegraph noise (RTN). At a fixed effective noise scale, the DM-assisted slow-switching protocol yields a superadditive transient ergotropy gain and near-maximal ergotropy during the initial charging stage, while the no-DM slow-switching control reaches comparable ergotropy only in a later revival. A finite superadditive region persists at fixed RTN amplitude, with protocol-dependent location and gain. In the Ising model, the enhancement is nonmonotonic in DM strength, with intermediate coupling giving near-optimal performance. Dressed-channel analysis associates this enhancement with changes in transition frequencies and longitudinal-noise matrix elements that reduce slow-RTN spectral weight. Superadditivity also persists in the tested anisotropic XY model.

apsDecisions.title: Space-efficient quantum solvers for Boolean satisfiability problems via structural reduction
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: The Boolean satisfiability (SAT) problem is a central benchmark for quantum optimization, but conventional encodings typically require one qubit per active variable, limiting their use on near-term quantum hardware. Here we introduce a space-efficient framework for one-in-three SAT based on the decisive chain reduction algorithm (DCRA), which exploits clause-induced dependences. For an instance generated with n variables and m clauses, let ñ be the number of active variables appearing in the clauses. The DCRA identifies s initial variables and expresses the remaining ñ−s active variables as linear combinations of them, reducing the effective search space from 2ñ to 2s. For positive random instances near the critical regime, we empirically find s close to ñ−m, yielding substantial qubit savings. In the reduced space, we derive a compact quadratic unconstrained binary optimization formulation whose problem Hamiltonian provides a common input for quantum annealing (QA), the quantum adiabatic algorithm (QAA), and the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA). Numerical simulations validate the framework on instances with up to 150 variables for QA-based solvers and up to 50 variables for QAA- and QAOA-based implementations. For QA-based solvers, finite-size scaling on satisfiable positive random instances with up to 200 variables shows an approximately exponential decay of the mean success probability and reveals a clause-density-dependent tradeoff between qubit reduction and annealing hardness. On a superconducting processor, the six-qubit QAOA solves a 25-variable instance with ñ=21 active variables, achieving 12.62% success above the 4.69% uniform-sampling baseline. For a 13-variable instance, the DCRA achieves a measured success probability of 3.37%, compared to 0.05% with the direct encoding at equal shot budgets. These results demonstrate that structure-exploiting reductions offer a practical route to qubit-efficient quantum formulations of satisfiability problems on near-term hardware.

apsDecisions.title: Hierarchy of entanglement detection criteria for random high-dimensional states
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Entanglement is a cornerstone in quantum information science, yet detecting it efficiently remains a challenging task. Focusing on states with nonpositive partial transpose, we establish a hierarchy among entropy-based, majorization, realignment, and reduction criteria for Haar uniformly generated random states in finite dimensions, analyzing their performance based on rank and subsystem dimension. We prove lower bounds on the rank of mixed quantum states beyond which the realignment and entropic criteria fail to detect entanglement. We evaluate the relative effectiveness of the considered detection methods using three key indicators—fraction of detected states, mean detectable entanglement, and minimum required entanglement. Our results provide insights into the entanglement thresholds needed for reliable detection, showing that, beyond a certain level of entanglement, all criteria become equally powerful for low-rank states, while a hierarchy emerges among the various criteria for moderate to high ranks. Intriguingly, the proposed ordering among the considered criteria in qubit-qudit systems is different from that in higher dimensions. Additionally, we establish that the detection efficiency is influenced by the asymmetry in the subsystem dimensions by illustrating how the realignment criterion behaves more efficiently than other detection methods when the difference between the subsystem dimensions is small.

apsDecisions.title: Hybrid analog-digital simulation of the Abelian Higgs model with transmon qutrits
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: To investigate gauge theories with near-term quantum computers warrants exploration of nontraditional quantum simulators to find resource-efficient simulation protocols and ultimately access exotic features of different field theories, including unexplored regimes of the QCD phase diagram. In this work, using superconducting transmon qutrit processors, we formulate and implement a pulse-based, three-level, hybrid analog-digital simulation protocol of the (1+1)-dimensional Abelian Higgs model (AHM) on two sites. Alongside this approach, we experimentally realize a gate-based implementation of the same model. Using the natural mapping of the three-level truncation of the transmon Hilbert space to the spin-1 truncated AHM, we observe real-time dynamics of AHM field observables, which are analogous to electric field operators, with both protocols. For the analog-digital protocol, we engineer a Floquet simulation with a combination of local analog drives, driven modification of the natural interaction Hamiltonian of the two transmons, and dynamical decoupling pulses. For the digital protocol, we use a state-of-the-art qutrit processor to implement a Trotterized simulation of the model incorporating advanced error mitigation techniques. We further discuss the scalability of the two approaches, and their potential to be extended to the simulation of other model Hamiltonians. Our experiments demonstrate a viable platform for future studies of spin-1- and SU(3)-based gauge theory models on current and near-term transmon qutrit processors.

apsDecisions.title: Rotational excitation of asymmetric-top molecular ions by electron impact: Application to H 2 O + , HDO + , and D 2 O +
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: The rotational excitation of the three asymmetric-top molecular ion isotopologues H2O+, HDO+, and D2O+ is studied theoretically using a combined framework of electron-molecule R matrix scattering theory, multichannel quantum-defect theory, frame transformation theory, and the Coulomb-Born approximation. The latter two have been adapted here for asymmetric-top rotors. State-resolved cross sections and kinetic rate coefficients for transitions from the rotational ground state of the ions are presented.

apsDecisions.title: Generation of perfectly achromatic optical vortices using a compensated tandem twisted nematic cell
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: In this work, we theoretically investigate a tandem crossed twisted nematic liquid crystal architecture for the generation of broadband (“white”) optical vortices. Operating in transmission, the system consists of two twisted nematic cells cascaded such that the liquid crystal director at the output of the first cell is strictly orthogonal to the director at the input of the second. Unlike conventional q-plates, this crossed configuration preserves the handedness of incident circularly polarized light. By rotating the entire polarization state by a target angle, the architecture imparts a corresponding spatial phase shift directly to the circular polarization. To evaluate its performance under realistic physical conditions, we develop a rigorous Jones matrix model. We systematically analyze the impact of deviations from the ideal waveguiding regime, manufacturing thickness mismatches, oblique incidence, and structural misalignments. By utilizing the modal overlap integral, we establish strict analytical figures of merit that provide a universal lower bound for the global mode purity. To mitigate the inherent amplitude and phase distortions, we propose three distinct operational strategies, ranging from parameter optimization to active phase correction. We demonstrate that active compensation effectively decouples the amplitude transmission efficiency from fabrication thickness tolerances, ensuring high optical throughput and superior phase fidelity. Ultimately, the direct structural compatibility of this architecture with emerging in-plane switching technologies establishes the tandem twisted nematic cell as a highly versatile blueprint for next-generation, fully dynamic broadband spatial light modulators.

apsDecisions.title: Invariant energy subspaces in quantum-optical high-harmonic generation: An information-theoretic approach
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Energy conservation is ubiquitous in the understanding of the process of high-harmonic generation. Yet a complete quantum-optical description of the photon-number-resolved structure implied by exact energy conservation remained elusive. Here, we solve this problem by introducing an information-theoretic perspective that separates the microscopic dynamics from the constraints imposed by energy conservation and only considers the imposed symmetry structure of the underlying state space. This leads to a decomposition into invariant eigenspace sectors of fixed energy, which we refer to as the energy-conserving subspaces of high-harmonic generation. The resulting weighted-photon-number sector structure is the Fock-space counterpart of the familiar harmonic energy-conservation condition and makes the photon-number correlations required by exact energy exchange between the participating field modes explicit. Energy conservation fixes the allowed support of the optical state, whereas the microscopic electron dynamics determine the amplitudes within this support. Coherent population of several allowed photon partitions can consequently generate intermode entanglement and nonclassical reduced states. More generally, the construction provides an information-theoretic description of symmetry constraints in strong-field processes without requiring a complete solution of the microscopic dynamics.

apsDecisions.title: Thermodynamics of a biophotomimetic nonreciprocal quantum battery
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We propose a theoretical model of a fully functional nonreciprocal quantum battery inspired by the architecture of bacterial light-harvesting complexes. We assign functional roles to collective quantum optical subradiant and superradiant states and introduce a unimodal cavity to assist storage. The collective bright- and dark-state energies and total effective decay rates are obtained from an effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian calculated using electromagnetic dyadic Green tensors. Upon varying the ring size, we find that work, flux, and power attain coincident maxima at the same intermediate ring size, whereas ergotropy reaches its maximum at a slightly larger ring size. The battery capacity is governed primarily by the ring size and depends weakly on the ring-central system coupling. Large coupling produces a pronounced finite-size optimum in ergotropy, whereas under weaker coupling the ergotropy increases monotonically with the battery capacity.

apsDecisions.title: Gaussian-amplitude transitions and Wigner phase-space dynamics of electron Airy beams in a uniform magnetic field
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Finite-energy electron Airy beams in a uniform magnetic field are investigated by reducing the transverse dynamics to a shifted one-dimensional harmonic oscillator. For an exponentially truncated Airy beam, an exact Airy-function representation of the propagated wave function is derived, and its asymptotic behavior at the characteristic moments of the magnetic period is examined. Near odd quarter periods, the Airy argument is driven toward the oscillatory sector, and direct evaluation of the Airy representation is therefore numerically delicate. To avoid this numerical difficulty, we further derive an exact Wigner representation, in which the dynamics appears as a rigid harmonic rotation in phase space and the position and momentum marginals remain stable throughout the magnetic period. For obstructed beams, the phase-space formulation is combined with a phase-sensitive similarity measure in a finite window. The analysis separates the Gaussian-amplitude transition, in which the state acquires a Gaussian envelope differing from the initial Airy state, from exact oscillator recurrence and uses Wigner regularization as a stable phase-space diagnostic; as an application, local self-healing is demonstrated for obstructed beams. The results show that the obstruction is not globally erased by the unitary evolution, but the surviving Airy components can locally reconstruct the beam profile within selected observation windows. This work provides a phase-space framework for evaluating structured electron beams in magnetic fields and offers a quantitative diagnostic for local self-healing in magnetically guided Airy beams.

apsDecisions.title: Ergotropy activation and coherence in dissipatively charged quantum batteries
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 原子分子光学或量子信息主题，未见目标晶体材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Quantum batteries can exploit quantum resources to enhance energy storage and work extraction, and recent experimental progress has brought their implementation closer to reality. In realistic settings, however, environmental dissipation is unavoidable, making dissipative charging a physically relevant operating regime. Here, we investigate ergotropy in dissipatively charged quantum batteries, focusing on interaction-induced work extraction. For two coupled two-level systems (TLSs), we derive exact analytical expressions for the total, coherent, and incoherent ergotropy in both resonant and detuned configurations. We show that in the resonant case, ergotropy is activated only above a critical coupling associated with an interaction-induced energy-level crossing, whereas detuning enables ergotropy already in the weak-coupling regime. Moreover, quantum coherence, although necessary for coherent work extraction, is not by itself sufficient to guarantee nonzero coherent ergotropy. In the strong-coupling regime, the resonant setup reaches the maximum ergotropy at a finite coupling strength, whereas the detuned setup approaches the same limit only asymptotically. Extending the analysis to a periodic XX spin chain of N TLSs, we analytically derive the finite-temperature coupling threshold for ergotropy activation and show that it scales as 1/N in the large-N limit. These results identify frequency detuning, interaction strength, and system size as key control parameters for ergotropy generation in open quantum batteries.

apsDecisions.title: Superheating field of clean superconductors near the type-I-type-II boundary: The low-temperature Meissner stability limit of niobium

detailFetch.abstract: We calculate the low-temperature superheating field $B_{\rm sh}$ of clean superconductors near the boundary between type-I and type-II superconductivity, with particular emphasis on Nb. Ginzburg–Landau theory is not applicable at low temperatures, while previous microscopic calculations have been limited to either the large- κ regime or the dirty limit. The clean, low- κ regime relevant to Nb has therefore remained unresolved. We solve the self-consistent nonlinear nonlocal Eilenberger problem for the Meissner state and then analyze its stability against small perturbations. For a Nb-like material with $\kappa_{\rm GL}=0.7$ , we obtain $B_{\rm sh}\simeq290\,{\rm mT}$ at T / T c = 0.2 , using $B_{c0}\simeq200\,{\rm mT}$ . For a TESLA-shaped Nb accelerator cavity, this corresponds to an intrinsic Meissner-stability limit of about $67\,{\rm MV/m}$ .

apsDecisions.title: Circular-mode optics for high-intensity beams and high-luminosity colliders
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 加速器束流/耦合器/腔体工程，未见目标材料生长和本征物性新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We study circular-mode optics as a framework for transporting and accelerating intrinsically flat beams while maintaining a round transverse projection in physical space. Motivated by the strong degradation of flat beams under low-energy space-charge forces, we develop a coupled-optics description of circular modes, analyze their formation and preservation, and derive lattice design conditions for conserving canonical angular momentum and coupling phase. These conditions motivate rotationally invariant transport and ring cells based on solenoids, symmetric alternating-gradient structures, and indexed dipoles. We further derive space-charge tune-shift and tune-spread expressions for circular-mode beams in uncoupled and coupled lattices, showing that they preserve the leading-order space-charge behavior of round beams while retaining intrinsic eigenemittance flatness. Particle-in-cell simulations with TRACK and impactx confirm the generation, transport, and acceleration of circular-mode beams in representative lattices, including regimes with strong space charge. Circular-mode optics therefore provides a promising route toward high-intensity hadron beams and high-luminosity collider applications.

apsDecisions.title: Direct large-area observation of subsurface plastic activity in conditioned copper electrodes
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 加速器束流/耦合器/腔体工程，未见目标材料生长和本征物性新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: High-field conditioning is the process by which radio-frequency structures in particle accelerators and other high-gradient devices reach their operating fields, yet the underlying physical mechanism remains an open question. Models and indirect measurements point to subsurface dislocation dynamics, but large-area structural measurements have been missing. We present electron backscatter diffraction measurements spanning millimeter-scale regions on a copper cathode conditioned at pulsed direct-current fields up to ∼80  MV/m in a sloped-anode geometry, which imposes a known gradient of field exposure across a single electrode. Across nine regions of interest spanning this exposure range, the mean intragrain misorientation of field-exposed regions exceeds that of unexposed references by ∼75%; the difference is reproduced by three independent misorientation metrics and confirmed by Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests. To our knowledge, this is the first large-area observation of structural differences between conditioned and unconditioned regions of a high-field electrode. The misorientation separates into three tiers (high-field center and edge, low-field periphery, and unexposed reference) that match the spatial profile of the conditioning-state variable ES predicted by Monte Carlo simulations. These observations point to the evolving subsurface dislocation population as a candidate physical basis of conditioning.

apsDecisions.title: Ferrite-SiC axially graded absorber for broadband higher-order mode damping and thermal response in a 1.5 GHz TM 020 -mode cavity
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 加速器束流/耦合器/腔体工程，未见目标材料生长和本征物性新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: The magnetic-field node of a TM020-mode cavity permits compact higher-order-mode (HOM) damping, but displacement of the coupling slots can expose the absorber to appreciable accelerating-mode leakage. A ferrite-SiC absorber is investigated numerically to combine broadband damping with improved thermomechanical response in a 1.5 GHz cavity. A transmission-line formulation relates material ordering to input impedance, and coaxial full-wave calculations show that placing SiC ahead of ferrite suppresses the pronounced low-frequency absorption dip of the reverse arrangement. The concept is integrated into a radially folded, six-sector absorber, with parameter sweeps resolving the effects of material dimensions, slot height, and sector angle. For the six higher-order modes (HOMs) tabulated, external quality factors are below 150, while the aligned accelerating mode has an external quality factor of 1.20×107. Frequency-resolved loss maps show increasing SiC participation across the transition near 2 GHz. At the same imposed absorber load of 2.65 kW, the hybrid reduces peak temperature rise from 97.0 to 79.9 K and maximum first principal stress in ferrite from 146.0 to 78.6 MPa, reductions of 17.6% and 46.2%, respectively. These results connect electromagnetic loss redistribution to improved thermal and mechanical response and support the hybrid arrangement as a compact damping option for TM020-mode cavities.

apsDecisions.title: Spatiospectral conditioning of laser-plasma-accelerated electron beams using electromagnetic solenoids
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 加速器束流/耦合器/腔体工程，未见目标材料生长和本征物性新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Microcoulomb-class electron beams from laser-plasma accelerators (LPAs) driven by kilojoule-class laser systems can enable high-flux electron radiography and copious secondary particle production. However, electron beam spatial properties such as transverse beam nonuniformity and large spatial scale at application sites can limit their utility. In this work, we demonstrate spatial conditioning of microcoulomb-class electron beams using electromagnetic solenoids as focusing optics. By applying ∼10  T solenoidal fields, we focused the electron beam onto a detection plane and measured a fluence enhancement factor of 6 over unconditioned electron beams. The chromatic focusing of the solenoids improved the resolution of electron beam radiographs produced using the focused electron beam. We also demonstrate a method using angled electromagnetic solenoids to simultaneously condition LPA electron beam spatial and spectral properties. These features are attractive for applications because they enable the spatial separation of a narrow-energy-spread population of the electron beam from the bulk of the electron beam.

apsDecisions.title: Achievement of continuous-wave 100 kW radiofrequency transmission by a 1.3 GHz high-power input coupler
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 加速器束流/耦合器/腔体工程，未见目标材料生长和本征物性新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: A high-power input coupler was developed at KEK to deliver 100 kW-class radiofrequency (rf) power in the continuous-wave (cw) mode at 1.3 GHz to a superconducting cavity. To mitigate thermal loads during high-power rf transmission, the coupler was engineered with active water cooling integrated into critical components, including a warm inner conductor, outer conductor, antenna, and rf window. The newly developed coupler underwent rf conditioning of up to 145 kW in the pulsed mode and 100 kW in the cw mode using a dedicated test stand at room temperature. The coupler successfully transmitted world-record cw 100 kW rf power at 1.3 GHz continuously for 10 h without any interlock event. During operation, the temperature rise of the warm inner conductor, the most thermally stressed component, was limited to 15 °C whereas the maximum observed temperature increase was 19 °C at the doorknob. Further power scaling was not constrained by the coupler itself. These results demonstrate that the newly developed coupler can reliably sustain cw rf transmissions exceeding 100 kW with excellent thermal performance.

apsDecisions.title: Longitudinal beam instability driven by coherent radiation in a steady-state microbunching laser modulator
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 加速器束流/耦合器/腔体工程，未见目标材料生长和本征物性新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Storage ring-based steady-state microbunching (SSMB) is a promising approach for generating high-average-power coherent radiation, while the instabilities driven by coherent undulator radiation in the laser modulator (LM) are important for the ring performance. In this paper, we investigate the longitudinal single-bunch multiturn LM instability using cavity-mode decomposition techniques. The evolution of the wakefield in the longitudinal beam dynamics equations is derived, and the instability growth rates are analyzed. Numerical simulations show excellent agreement with the theoretical model, validating the mode-decomposition approach. These findings provide critical insights into the design and operation of SSMB storage rings, suggesting effective mitigation strategies to suppress the instability and enhance the overall performance.

apsDecisions.title: Emittance preservation under multifaceted CSR effects in isochronous deflection structures for multikiloampere bunches
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 加速器束流/耦合器/腔体工程，未见目标材料生长和本征物性新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: In modern accelerator facilities, coherent synchrotron radiation (CSR) presents a fundamental limitation to maintaining high-brightness electron-beam quality during deflection, with accurate modeling of its effects remaining an outstanding challenge. This study introduces a novel optimization method using an integral approach to suppress CSR-induced transverse emittance degradation under two representative bunch scenarios: ultrashort bunches and high-charge long bunches. We present analytical solutions for suppressing CSR effects in the dipoles across several quadruple-bend-achromat (QBA) layouts and establish general conditions for mitigating CSR-induced emittance growth in the subsequent drift sections of isochronous beamlines. Our analysis demonstrates that the QBA is the minimal configuration capable of simultaneously suppressing transverse emittance degradation and preserving the longitudinal beam distribution. Beam tracking results show negligible emittance growth for multikiloampere bunches at a 16° deflection. Furthermore, multicell simulation confirms the exact scalability of this approach. While previous designs suffer severe emittance degradation upon cascading, the QBA maintains exceptionally preserved beam quality.

apsDecisions.title: Zn 2 + and Mn 2 + doping effect on spin dynamics of Fe 3 O 4 -based magnetic nanoparticles: A possible path to efficient MRI contrast agents
apsDecisions.selectionReason: Zn/Mn掺杂Fe₃O₄纳米粒自旋动力学，偏MRI应用候补。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Iron oxide-based magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) play a major role as contrast agents for magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). The introduction of Zn2+ and Mn2+ ions within their crystal lattice alters the magnetic anisotropy and the spin dynamical properties of the systems, which in turn influence the nuclear relaxation mechanisms that drive contrast enhancement in MRI. This work explored two sets of doped-magnetite MNPs (chemical formula ZnxMnyFe3−x−yO4) with core diameters of d∼4 or 15 nm produced by the fast and reproducible microwave-assisted synthesis method, and using different solvents like water or polyols. The d∼4  nm MNPs were doped with Zn2+, from x=0 to 0.9; for Zn2+=0.5, Mn2+ was introduced at y=0.2,0.4. The d∼15  nm MNPs were doped with Zn2+ from x=0 to 0.4, with Mn2+ added at y=0.1 for Zn2+=0.3 and at 0.3 for Zn2+=0.4. Both sets were dispersed in water with carboxymethyl-dextran or polyacrylic acid coatings to ensure their colloidal stability, even under high magnetic fields. We highlighted the influence of the size and of the Zn2+/Mn2+ doping on the static and dynamical magnetic properties, also through the H1-NMR-dispersion profile analysis over a wide frequency range and the application of the superparamagnetic relaxation heuristic model. Larger particles exhibited higher nuclear relaxometric efficiency and anisotropy compared to the smaller ones, consistently outperforming the commercial contrast agents. On the other hand, the magnetic response and the nuclear relaxivities are enhanced by a Zn2+ content of x=0.1 ions for approximately 4  nm MNPs and of x=0.4 for approximately 15  nm MNPs, while a slight enhancing effect was obtained by Mn2+ introduction. It is thus shown how a proper size and doping combination provide an attractive way to modify the static and dynamical magnetic properties of MNPs by acting on different spin-spin correlation times dominating in specific frequency intervals, thus enabling the fine-tuning of image contrast properties suitable for magnetic resonance imaging.

apsDecisions.title: Simultaneous determination of local magnetic fields and sensor orientation with nitrogen-vacancy centers in nanodiamond
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 涉及凝聚态/材料相关关键词，但尚未确证直接实验生长或目标物性的新证据；保留候补，不能仅据标题称已排除。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in nanodiamonds have emerged as a promising quantum sensing platform for biomedical imaging applications, yet random orientations of individual particles present significant challenges in large-scale sensor calibration. In this study, we demonstrate a novel approach to simultaneously determine each particle’s crystallographic axes and the surrounding local vector magnetic field. Specifically, a minimum of four distinct bias fields is required to unambiguously extract both the orientation and the local field. We validate our method experimentally using NV centers in two scenarios: (i) in a bulk diamond with known crystal orientation as a proof of concept and (ii) on various single nanodiamonds to mimic real-world applications. Our work represents a crucial step toward unlocking the full potential of nanodiamonds for advanced applications such as in situ biomedical imaging and nanoscale sensing in complex environments.

apsDecisions.title: Generation of perfect spatiotemporal acoustic vortices
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 涉及凝聚态/材料相关关键词，但尚未确证直接实验生长或目标物性的新证据；保留候补，不能仅据标题称已排除。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Spatiotemporal (ST) vortices carrying transverse orbital angular momentum have attracted growing interest in both optics and acoustics. However, despite diverse generation schemes, a fundamental limitation persists: the vortex radius increases with the topological charge, leading to a size mismatch that complicates efficient multiplexing and detection. Here, we introduce the concept of perfect ST acoustic vortices to decouple the vortex size from the topological charge. Unlike conventional counterparts, these vortices maintain a nearly constant radius regardless of the topological charge. We theoretically construct this new class of vortices via the Fourier transform of an ST Bessel-Gaussian spectrum in the wave-vector-frequency domain. Experimentally, we implement the synthesis using a one-dimensional acoustic phased array. We then characterize the generated fields, confirming their size invariance and investigating their propagation and superposition properties. By enabling a nearly charge-independent vortex radius, our work overcomes a critical constraint of ST acoustic vortices, paving the way for high-capacity acoustic communications, sensing, and particle manipulation.

apsDecisions.title: Measurement-induced state transitions across the fluxonium qubit landscape
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Understanding the mechanisms that limit high-fidelity readout in circuit quantum electrodynamics is essential for its optimization. Multiphoton resonances are understood to be a limiting factor, causing population transfer from the computational states to higher-energy states under drive. This effect, known as measurement-induced state transitions, has been extensively studied for the transmon qubit. While this exploration has begun for the fluxonium qubit, a systematic study of this effect is lacking. Here, we bridge this gap by theoretically studying measurement-induced state transitions in the fluxonium qubit over a wide range of parameters, comprising essentially all experimentally explored ranges. We find that lighter fluxoniums are less susceptible to these state transitions when compared with their heavier counterparts. We attribute this effect to the combination of lower density of multiphoton resonances, a smaller requisite coupling for a given dispersive shift, and a more harmoniclike structure of the charge operator. We confirm the validity of our analysis by performing time-dependent readout simulations. Finally, we consider the impact of the superinductor’s array modes on measurement-induced state transitions over a large range of parameters.

apsDecisions.title: Deterministically addressing spins at clock transitions with a frequency- and bandwidth-tunable superconducting resonator
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 超导谐振器调谐clock-transition自旋寻址，偏量子测量方法候补。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Solid-state spin ensembles addressed via superconducting circuits are promising candidates for quantum memory applications, offering multimodal storage capability and second-long coherence times at their clock transition. Implementing practical memory schemes requires dynamic control over both the resonator frequency and bandwidth, and most crucially, deterministic access to the clock transitions. In this article, we report measurements of a superconducting resonator whose frequency can be tuned by passing a DC current through the high-kinetic-inductance thin film, and whose bandwidth can be tuned by parametric coupling to a low-Q buffer resonator. Using this resonator, we deterministically address an ensemble of bismuth donors at their clock transition, measuring a Hahn-echo coherence time of 450 ms. We demonstrate RF driving of the bismuth donor hyperfine transitions, as well as dynamic bandwidth control of the resonator.

apsDecisions.title: Muonium dynamics as a probe for depth-resolved properties of 4 H − SiC
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 4H-SiC深度分辨muonium探针，缺陷表征方法候补。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: This study establishes a baseline for muonium (Mu) charge-exchange dynamics in n-type 4H−SiC through a detailed low-energy muon spin rotation (LE−μSR) investigation. Epitaxially grown and ion-implanted samples with nitrogen and phosphorus donors were characterized to assess the effect of carrier concentration and doping method on defect formation. LE−μSR enabled nanometer-scale depth profiling of near-surface and implanted regions, revealing variations in charge carrier concentration due to fixed surface charges. The temperature dependence of the diamagnetic fraction and phase provided direct evidence of the Mu0 to Mu− transition, with extracted activation energies consistent with known donor ionization energies. Additionally, high-field μSR was used to analyze the Mu dynamics, and Monte Carlo simulations were used to model the Mu0 electron capture process. The simulation results offer a quantitative method to extract free electron concentrations from LE−μSR data, enhancing its capability to characterize the activation of dopants and carrier depth profiles. We demonstrate that LE−μSR is a powerful depth-resolved tool that can provide insights for optimizing the fabrication of reliable SiC devices for power electronics.

apsDecisions.title: Adiabatic self-vibrations generated by inelastic Andreev tunneling in a movable Cooper-pair box
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Self-sustained oscillators produce stable periodic motion robust to dissipation. Such motion is usually achieved by work fed back into the oscillator, but its performance is often limited by frequency-dependent operation. Here, we propose a scheme for self-sustained vibrations without external feedback. We consider a movable Cooper-pair box attached to the free end of a voltage-biased normal-metal pillar. The Cooper-pair box carries an Andreev current subject to an electric field applied perpendicular to the current. In the adiabatic limit, where the Cooper-pair box state follows its motion, vibrational instability occurs, pumped by inelastic Andreev tunneling. Nonlinearity of the Josephson coupling saturates the vibrational amplitude, resulting in two-dimensional self-vibrations. We discuss the advantage of this adiabatic scheme in comparison with feedback-induced self-oscillation.

apsDecisions.title: Dispersive mode coupling in p -doped semiconductor nanomechanical resonators
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Dispersive coupling between vibrational modes with different frequencies is a major nonlinear dynamical effect. We show, analytically and numerically, that in p-doped semiconductors such coupling can be strongly enhanced. Moreover, the relative coupling strength increases with the order of the nonlinearity. The doping-induced dispersive coupling becomes much stronger than the intrinsic one already for moderately strong doping. Its dependence on the hole density is nonmonotonic, and the temperature dependence becomes nonmonotonic for higher densities. Relevant mesoscopic frequency fluctuations are briefly discussed. The theory is applied to Si resonators, where doping is often used to compensate the temperature dependence of a clock mode, whereas another low-frequency mode is used as a thermometer to enable temperature stabilization.

apsDecisions.title: Planar multiplexed elastic-wave bound states in the continuum in two-dimensional Lamb-wave phononic crystal plates
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 涉及凝聚态/材料相关关键词，但尚未确证直接实验生长或目标物性的新证据；保留候补，不能仅据标题称已排除。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Bound states in the continuum (BICs) enable elastic-wave resonances with ultralow radiation loss, but in multimode plates, localized modes readily couple to multiple radiation channels. Here we extend a symmetry-mismatch design recently implemented in one-dimensional Lamb-wave structures to a two-dimensional phononic crystal plate and realize elastic BICs and quasi-BICs by exploiting a mismatch between symmetric (S) and antisymmetric (A) Lamb modes. The plate is engineered such that the A mode forms a passband while the S mode exhibits a band gap; a central defect then hosts localized S modes whose eigenfrequencies lie in this band gap yet overlap the A-mode continuum, forming S-mode BICs. Finite-element simulations and laser Doppler vibrometry show that the number of BIC modes can be controlled by varying the number of defect unit cells. By weakly breaking the midplane mirror symmetry through tilted hole sidewalls, we induce controlled S−A hybridization and convert these strictly bound states into quasi-BICs that are efficiently excited by plane waves. Using this mechanism, we implement a planar multicavity structure where spatially separated quasi-BIC resonators are addressed at distinct frequencies, thereby realizing planar space-frequency multiplexing and providing a simple route to multifrequency elastic-wave signal processing and integrated phononic circuits.

apsDecisions.title: Simulation-guided design of an integrated photonic cavity for frequency-multiplexed spontaneous parametric down-conversion
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Frequency-multiplexed entangled photon pair sources with narrow bandwidths and high pair generation efficiency are a key enabling technology for quantum networking. We present a simulation-based design study of an integrated photonic racetrack resonator source for spontaneous parametric down-conversion (SPDC) that simultaneously achieves all three properties. The central result is a simulated set of 90 doubly resonant signal and idler frequency-mode pairs with an effective frequency-space Schmidt number of 89.62, an average single-island purity of 0.960, an average bandwidth of 1.08 GHz, a mean free spectral range of 51.9 GHz, and a total internal pair-generation-rate efficiency of 1.16  GHz mW−1. Under deterministic wavelength-based splitting, the folded 45-pair state has an effective frequency-space Schmidt number of 44.93. To support these predictions, we derive a closed-form analytical connection between classical cavity parameters (resonant frequencies, decay rates, and coupling coefficients) and the quantum joint spectral amplitude and pair generation rate, extending the dispersive-medium quantization formalism of Raymer to the nonlinear optical cavity case. We demonstrate how classical electromagnetic field simulations can be combined with this analytical framework to predict quantum figures of merit for an integrated photonic source prior to fabrication. Fabrication and experimental validation are left for future work.

apsDecisions.title: Synthetic area spread in two-dimensional arrays of superconducting quantum interference filters
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 涉及凝聚态/材料相关关键词，但尚未确证直接实验生长或目标物性的新证据；保留候补，不能仅据标题称已排除。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Superconducting quantum interference devices (SQUIDs), formed by incorporating Josephson junctions into loops of superconducting material, are the backbone of many modern quantum sensing systems. It has been demonstrated that, by combining multiple SQUID loops into a two-dimensional (2D) array, it is possible to fabricate ultrahigh-performing radio-frequency sensors. However, to function as absolute magnetometers, current-in-use arrays require the area of each SQUID loop in the array to be incommensurate. In doing so forbids the achievement of their full potential of performance, limited only by the standard quantum limit. This is because imposing incommensurability in the areas contrasts with optimized performance in each single SQUID loop. In this work, we report that by selectively inserting “bare” sections of a superconducting circuit with no Josephson junctions, 2D SQUID arrays can operate as an absolute magnetometer even when no physical area spread is applied. Based on a generalization of currently available theories, a complete analytical formulation for the one-to-one correspondence between the distribution of these bare loops and what we call a “synthetic area spread” is unveiled. This synthetic spread represents the equivalent physical spread of incommensurate SQUID loops that you would use to obtain the absolute voltage-magnetic flux response if no bare loops were in use. Our work opens the way to a broader use of this technology for the fabrication of ultrahigh-performance absolute quantum sensors. Our approach is also experimentally verified by fabricating several 2D superconducting quantum interference filter arrays incorporating bare superconducting loops and by demonstrating that they behave in alignment with what is suggested by our theory.

apsDecisions.title: Tailoring the properties of YBa 2 Cu 3 O 7 − δ thin films by 30-keV He + irradiation: An enabling route to superconducting-device nanopatterning
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 30keV He⁺调控YBCO薄膜的超导器件纳米图形化；实验超导材料调控强相关。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Focused helium ion beam (He-FIB) irradiation with 30-keV ions is a key tool for nanoscale patterning and defect engineering in high-transition temperature (Tc) cuprate superconducting devices, yet its usable fluence window is constrained by the competing requirements of reliable superconductivity suppression and minimal structural degradation. In this work, we provide a comprehensive dataset on the effects of large-area 30-keV He+ ion exposure on the electric transport and superconducting properties of epitaxial YBa2Cu3O7−δ (YBCO) thin films. X-ray diffraction shows a fluence-driven loss of crystalline order accompanied by an out-of-plane lattice expansion and an orthorhombic-to-tetragonal transition, culminating in predominant amorphization at the highest fluence of 1×1016  cm−2. Raman spectra exhibit increasing disorder while lacking signatures of oxygen depletion, indicating that irradiation mainly generates oxygen-related Frenkel defects rather than changing the carrier concentration. Consistently, with increasing fluence, the normal-state resistivity ρN(T) at temperature T above Tc increases strongly, while ∂ρN/∂T remains nearly unchanged at moderate fluence. The suppression of Tc is accurately described by Abrikosov–Gor’kov pair breaking and reaches complete quenching of superconductivity at 4.5×1015  cm−2. The anisotropic upper critical fields decrease approximately exponentially with increasing fluence; the vortex activation energy is reduced, and the anisotropy drops, in contrast to oxygen-depleted YBCO. Hall-angle analysis confirms a nearly constant carrier density but a systematic increase in defect scattering and reduced mobility, consistent with a crossover toward the dirty limit at high fluence. These results establish quantitative fluence thresholds and a practical operational window for He-FIB nanopatterning of YBCO quantum circuits.

apsDecisions.title: Magnetic microscopy of skyrmions in magnetic thin films with chiral overlayers
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 带手性覆盖层磁薄膜中的skyrmion磁成像；实验磁纹理强相关。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Topologically nontrivial magnetic textures such as skyrmions offer promising opportunities for spintronic applications. In recent years, it has been shown that the magnetic properties of layered materials can be affected by depositing chiral molecules on the surface, while the influence of chiral overlayers on skyrmion properties such as their stability and interactions remains largely unexplored. To address this challenge, we employ wide-field nitrogen-vacancy (N−V) magnetometry to directly image skyrmions in chiral-molecule-functionalized magnetic thin films, enabling quantitative mapping of magnetic stray fields over extended areas under ambient conditions. Using pixel-resolved optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) combined with controlled magnetic fields, we reproducibly nucleate and probe skyrmion states in CoFeB ferromagnetic samples, enabling quantitative investigation of their properties. We observe indications of enantioselective and magnetic-field-polarity-dependent modifications of skyrmion properties suggesting possible chirality-dependent modifications of topological spin textures and motivating future theoretical investigations of the underlying coupling mechanisms.

apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We present experimental evidence of a thermally driven amplitude-frequency nonlinearity in a thin-film quartz phononic crystal resonator at millikelvin temperatures. The nonlinear response arises from the coupling of the mechanical mode to an ensemble of microscopic two-level system (TLS) defects driven out of equilibrium by the microwave readout signal. In contrast to the conventional Duffing oscillator, the observed nonlinearity exhibits a mixed reactive-dissipative character. Notably, the reactive effect can manifest as either a softening or hardening of the mechanical resonance, depending on the ratio of thermal to phonon energy. By combining the standard TLS theory with a thermal conductance model, the measured power-dependent response is quantitatively reproduced, and readout-enhanced relaxation damping from off-resonant TLSs is identified as the primary mechanism limiting mechanical coherence. Within this framework, we delineate the conditions under which similar systems will realize this nonlinearity.

apsDecisions.title: High-pressure synthesis of indium polynitride InN 10 with structurally diverse polynitrogen frameworks

detailFetch.abstract: Polymeric nitrogen frameworks are of interest for high-energy-density materials because their conversion to molecular N2 is associated with substantial energy release, while their experimental synthesis remains challenging. Here we combine particle-swarm structure prediction, first-principles calculations, and laser-heated diamond-anvil-cell experiments to investigate the phase stability and bonding of the In–N system under pressure. Two pressure-stabilized InN10 polymorphs were obtained experimentally, with in situ synchrotron X-ray diffraction and Raman spectroscopy supporting their assignment to tetragonal I4 at 55 GPa and orthorhombic Ama2 at 80 GPa. The I4 phase contains isolated pentazolate N5 rings, whereas the Ama2 structure contains an extended chain–ladder nitrogen framework involving N17-based motifs. Electronic-structure and bonding analyses indicate substantial charge transfer from indium to the nitrogen sublattice, with the dominant bonding contributions arising from covalent N–N interactions. The calculated energetic metrics show that Ama2 InN10 has a higher volumetric energy density than the other predicted In–N phases, associated with its higher packing density and extended nitrogen connectivity. The results establish two pressure-stabilized InN10 polymorphs with distinct ring-based and chain–ladder polynitrogen frameworks and clarify the role of indium in stabilizing different nitrogen connectivities under pressure.

apsDecisions.title: Voltage-tunable Josephson diode at zero applied field

detailFetch.abstract: We report a gate-tunable Josephson diode effect in hybrid nanowire junctions consisting of a spin-orbit-coupled semiconductor core coated with epitaxial ferromagnetic insulator and superconductor shells. The wires display a hysteretic superconducting window as a function of axial magnetic field. In the superconducting regime, the devices exhibit nonreciprocal supercurrent transport, with the diode efficiency showing a strong dependence on back-gate voltage. The effect persists at zero applied magnetic field in a remanent magnetization state following a controlled demagnetization procedure. These findings demonstrate a voltage-controlled Josephson diode in a single junction and suggest a route toward probing intrinsically broken inversion and time-reversal symmetries in hybrid materials.

apsDecisions.title: Electronic structure and oxidation states in high-pressure synthesized isostructural CeCN 5 and TbCN 5

detailFetch.abstract: Understanding the behavior of 4 f electrons in materials containing rare earth elements is one of the fundamental questions within condensed matter physics. In this work the electronic properties of isostructural CeCN 5 and TbCN 5 , both recently synthesized at extreme pressure, are investigated using Density Functional Theory (DFT) calculations. We include the on-site Coulomb repulsion between localized 4 f states within the static DFT+U framework; the DFT+U results are cross-checked with DFT+dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) calculations within the quasi-atomic (Hubbard-I) approximation. Despite CeCN 5 and TbCN 5 being isostructural compounds Ce and Tb show different oxidation states, 4+ and 3+ respectively. This leads to distinctly different electronic properties: the former compound is an insulator, while the latter is a metal. An extra electron which is donated by Ce to the polymeric C-N network is distributed across the network. This leads to a modification of the bond length in CeCN 5 compared to TbCN 5 . Still, the polymeric C-N networks can accommodate the different oxidation states in isostructural lanthanide-carbon-nitrogen (LnCN) compounds. Our results underline that LnCN compounds under high pressure offer a unique platform for probing the interplay between 4 f -electron behavior and structural complexity.

apsDecisions.selectionReason: 涉及凝聚态/材料相关关键词，但尚未确证直接实验生长或目标物性的新证据；保留候补，不能仅据标题称已排除。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We theoretically investigate a tunable and suppressible non-Hermitian skin effect (NHSE) in lattice systems governed by non-Abelian SU(2) gauge fields, Zeeman field, and spin-dependent gain and loss. We show that non-Abelian hopping alone can generate a parity-dependent discrepancy between open- and periodic-boundary spectra, even in the absence of the NHSE. A uniform Zeeman field or spin-dependent gain and loss activates a direction-selective NHSEs, whereas their coexistence gives rise to a bipolar NHSE. Strikingly, we find that a spatially nonuniform Zeeman field generically suppresses the NHSE and drives boundary-accumulated skin modes back into the bulk, irrespective of the modulation profile. This suppression originates from the competition between skin-induced boundary accumulation and gradient-induced Wannier–Stark-like localization. Our results reveal versatile and experimentally accessible mechanisms for engineering, tuning, and suppressing non-Hermitian boundary localization, and provide a promising route toward exploring non-Abelian non-Hermitian physics in platforms such as electrical circuits.

apsDecisions.title: Néel-vector-orientation induced direction-robust spin filtering in two-dimensional altermagnets
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 涉及凝聚态/材料相关关键词，但尚未确证直接实验生长或目标物性的新证据；保留候补，不能仅据标题称已排除。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Whether an antiferromagnet can host direction-robust spin-polarized transport without a conventional spin-selective band gap remains a central challenge in antiferromagnetic spintronics. Here, we establish a gapless, direction-robust spin-filtering mechanism in a compensated two-dimensional altermagnetic Weyl semimetal that requires neither a spin-selective band gap nor a large velocity contrast between spin projections. Using Janus monolayer Ta2TeSeO as a realistic platform, we combine symmetry analysis with first-principles calculations, full-Brillouin-zone Wannier interpolation, and semiclassical transport. Rotating the Néel vector removes a unitary-mirror constraint and shifts one Weyl-cone pair away from its parent high-symmetry line. For an in-plane Néel vector, the residual C2zT symmetry forbids the independent σy mass that would open a local gap, allowing the reconstructed cones to shift in momentum while remaining gapless. Breaking unitary C2z simultaneously lifts the energy equivalence of the remaining mirror-pinned Weyl cones. The resulting coexistence of a metallic spin-projected manifold and a low-density-of-states (DOS) Weyl-derived manifold produces a predominantly DOS-driven conductance imbalance. At charge neutrality and 20 K, the longitudinal conductivity polarization for n∥x remains positive for every in-plane current direction and ranges from 76.4% to 82.0%. The symmetry-related in-plane Néel orientations provide two distinct spin-filtering states. This Néel-vector-driven symmetry mechanism provides a general route to direction-robust gapless spin filtering in compensated altermagnets.

apsDecisions.title: Coexistence of magnon-induced optical vortex and Gaussian beam scattering assisted by rotational umklapp process
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 磁晶体光学Brillouin散射实验，旋转umklapp交换角动量；磁光候补。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: The exploitation of crystal-lattice symmetries to engineer angular momentum transfer between structured light and magnons marks a novel frontier for optomagnonic research. In Brillouin light scattering, when focused light propagates parallel to an external magnetic field and interacts with ferromagnetic uniform magnons, only optical vortex scattering is expected to be permitted. Due to the combined effects of magneto-optical coupling and optical spin-orbit interaction, the transfer of magnon spin angular momentum to photon orbital angular momentum allows for this distinctive scattering phenomenon. Here, we experimentally demonstrate that, for a specific ferromagnetic crystal orientation, Gaussian beam scattering coexists with the optical vortex scattering, contrary to conventional expectations based on angular momentum conservation between magnons and photons. We show that the crystal lattice, via the rotational umklapp process, provides the missing angular momentum required for the Gaussian beam scattering. Furthermore, our theoretical model predicts a focus-dependent efficiency crossover between Gaussian beam and optical vortex scattering as the numerical aperture increases.

apsDecisions.title: First-principles prediction of infrared optical properties of insulators using a resonant photon-phonon interaction model

apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We present a simplified formalism for predicting infrared optical constants from first-principles calculations by considering resonant interaction between infrared photons and the crystal lattice. Addressing limitations of the widely used four-parameter semiquantum Lorentz model, the proposed approach bridges the gap between the harmonic three-parameter model and the rigorous many-body Green's-function-based approaches. By incorporating essential anharmonic effects including four-phonon scattering and phonon renormalization, the model provides an efficient and accurate alternative while maintaining low computational cost. The frequency-dependent refractive indices of MgO and rutile TiO2 are computed and compared with experimental data, demonstrating good quantitative agreement. The framework offers a practical approach for predicting optical properties of materials across a wide range of materials.

apsDecisions.title: Directional selection of field-induced phases by weak anisotropy in triangular-lattice K 2 Mn ( SeO 3 ) 2
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 三角晶格K₂Mn(SeO₃)₂的单晶/粉末中子、热力学和定向场诱导磁相；实验强相关。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Triangular-lattice systems host a variety of ground states, ranging from quantum spin liquids to magnetically ordered phases, the latter of which can exhibit a sequence of magnetic phase transitions under applied magnetic fields. Here, we report magnetic and thermodynamic measurements, combined with powder and single-crystal neutron diffraction, on a high-spin, nearly isotropic Mn2+ triangular-lattice system K2Mn(SeO3)2. The compound undergoes long-range magnetic ordering below TN∼4K in zero field. Contrary to expectations for an ideal Heisenberg system, an up-down-zero (UD0) magnetic structure is favored down to the lowest temperature (0.05 K), rather than the commonly expected Y-type structure. This UD0 state is, however, highly sensitive to external magnetic fields. For fields applied along the c axis, it is readily destabilized and replaced by the Y-type structure, followed by an up-up-down (UUD) phase corresponding to the 1/3 magnetization plateau. In contrast, when the field is applied within the triangular plane, the system evolves into a canted Y state at a higher critical field. These results reveal that weak anisotropy, though small in magnitude, exerts a strongly orientation-dependent influence, playing a key role in selecting the field-induced phases in this frustrated magnet.
