apsDecisions.title: Complex dynamics in the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick game
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We study the outcome of adaptive learning among many players engaged in sets of two-strategy, two-player games. We are interested in typical games and therefore generate the payoff matrices randomly at the outset. These payoff matrices then remain fixed throughout the learning process. This provides a game-theoretic foundation for the Sherrington-Kirkpatrick (SK) game recently introduced by Garnier-Brun et al. [Phys. Rev. X 14, 021039 (2024)]. The original model studied by these authors corresponds to the special case with no bias toward either strategy. Here, we determine the stability of learning in SK games with general random biases and show that the nature of the stable state is affected by random fields. We also introduce a grand-canonical version of the SK game, in which players may choose to abstain. For this extended model, we again determine the stability of learning. Our analysis confirms that complex situations involving many players are often unlearnable, even if each player chooses between only two actions. The rate at which players forget past payoffs and the competitiveness of the game emerge as key parameters determining whether learning converges to a unique fixed point, whether multiple fixed points arise, or whether the dynamics remain persistently volatile.

apsDecisions.title: Minimal representations of topology-preserving quantumlike states
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We provide an equitable partition that gives an exact, minimal representation for the graph Cartesian product formed from quantumlike bits that preserves the relevant spectral and topological properties. We show that this result follows from the fact that the operations of taking the Cartesian product of graphs and constructing equitable partition of the graphs commute. Numerical simulations illustrate the preserved emergent eigenstates in the reduced structures. Additionally, we provide a construction of the minimal structure without passing through the Cartesian product. Finally, we frame quantumlike structures in the language of topology and fibrations.

apsDecisions.title: Constrained surrogates for arbitrary families of continuous probability distributions
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Empirical regularities described by parametrized families of probability distributions can shape how complex systems are interpreted and explained. A recurring problem is to determine the extent to which these descriptions are supported by observations, and how they can be used to characterize the underlying system. Here we introduce a general framework for constructing constrained surrogates capable of representing arbitrary families of continuous distributions. We demonstrate its utility by providing explicit algorithms for several canonical distributions in statistical physics, including continuous power-law, lognormal, exponential, and truncated Gaussian distributions. These constrained surrogates enable unbiased estimation and accurate tests of model validity based on arbitrary (physically meaningful) sample statistics, without requiring specification or estimation of model parameters. We show how these theoretical advantages translate into more informative and nuanced conclusions in applications ranging from bushfire magnitudes and word usage in texts to brain connectomes and city populations.

apsDecisions.title: Generalized Schamel nonlinear Schrödinger dynamics of ion-acoustic wave packets in electronegative plasmas with trapped negative ions
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We investigate the amplitude modulation of ion-acoustic wave packets in an unmagnetized electronegative plasma composed of cold positive ions, Boltzmann electrons, and negative ions following a Schamel trapped-particle distribution. The trapped-particle description is relevant to weakly collisional electronegative plasmas supporting Bernstein–Greene–Kruskal (BGK)-type potential structures and ion-hole equilibria, where a fraction of the negative-ion population can become trapped in the self-consistent wave potential. Unlike conventional analytic closures (Boltzmann, Tsallis, κ-distributed, nonthermal), which we show can only produce a cubic envelope nonlinearity regardless of their parametrization, this nonanalytic trapped-particle response naturally yields a generalized Schamel nonlinear Schrödinger equation combining the familiar cubic term with a genuinely noninteger |Ψ|1/2Ψ contribution. Derived through both a long-wavelength (Gardner-Schamel) limit and the full modulated-wave-packet limit, the resulting dispersion, cubic, and fractional coefficients are obtained in closed form. Two results stand out. First, the maximum modulational growth rate depends nonmonotonically on the negative-ion concentration, exhibiting an interior optimum that maximizes the instability above a critical temperature ratio, and, near the long-wavelength threshold, a finite concentration window outside of which the instability vanishes entirely. Second, a split-step Fourier analysis shows that the trapped-ion population breaks the time-symmetry of the Peregrine and Akhmediev rogue-wave solutions, causing them to build up faster than they decay, a signature invisible in the peak amplitude alone. These results extend previous electronegative plasma models and provide testable predictions for nonlinear wave localization in plasmas containing trapped particles.

apsDecisions.title: Link length and energy fluctuations in extensible freely jointed chains
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: The freely jointed chain is often applied to model the thermodynamics of single polymer chains, but the traditional formulation of the model lacks internal energy changes due to bond stretching. For this reason, the extensible freely jointed chain model includes a potential energy function, typically harmonic, that governs the length of each link in the chain. Among the other quantities of interest that are subject to thermal fluctuations, these link lengths and energies too fluctuate about their ensemble-average values. Since a plethora of models for polymer chains and networks incorporate chain dissociation as a function of either link length or energy, these fluctuations are crucial to understand and quantify. Motivated by this fact, fluctuations in link length and energy are analyzed within a freely jointed chain under an applied force. These fluctuations are quantified through their average values, standard deviations, and probability distributions. Across all values, asymptotically correct analytic relations and their less ergonomic exact counterparts are introduced. The asymptotic relations are verified to be accurate through direct comparison and to be correct within transcendentally small terms through error analysis. In certain cases, the fluctuations are shown to be approximately normally distributed. Hereafter, model components predicated on link length or energy ought to account for these fluctuations.

apsDecisions.title: Hidden square order through orientational-domain reorganization during nonequilibrium expansion of colloidal systems
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We investigate the expansion dynamics of two-dimensional colloidal assemblies interacting through a competing potential that supports unconventional local ordering. The systems are initially prepared under logarithmic confinement and subsequently released, generating a nonequilibrium decompression process. We show that expansion is not a simple disordering mechanism. Instead, the system undergoes a rich structural reorganization in which an initially dominant hexagonal core progressively shrinks while square local environments emerge and proliferate in the surrounding region. By combining real-space analysis, structure factors, bond-orientational order parameters, mean-square displacement, and dynamic exponents, we demonstrate that the expansion process promotes the formation and reorganization of square domains whose orientations initially reflect the sixfold geometry of the central hexagonal nucleus. This orientational-domain organization strongly influences the evolution of global order through cancellation effects between domains with different orientations. Finite-temperature simulations and independent thermal realizations further show that the structural conversion is robust, whereas the detailed late-time mobility events are trajectory dependent. As a consequence, substantial amounts of square local order may remain hidden from conventional global order parameters, demonstrating that local and global measures of structural order can become strongly decoupled during nonequilibrium expansion.

apsDecisions.title: Geometry-induced shifts in dielectric-loss peaks of amorphous ices
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Dielectric relaxation times of powdered amorphous ices have served as kinetic benchmarks for the glass dynamics of water. To examine the effect of sample geometry on the dielectric spectra, we measured in situ dielectric spectra of bulk and emulsified high- and low-density amorphous ices at P≃0.01GPa. The emulsified samples showed loss maxima in the measurement window, while the bulk samples showed none. This is consistent with the qualitative peak-shift trends calculated using series-capacitor and Maxwell-Wagner-Sillars approximations for ice and oil. Caution is needed when using the dielectric results obtained from emulsionlike samples (e.g., powder) as kinetic benchmarks.

apsDecisions.title: Nonlinear Brownian motions in gases: Kinetic equations and relaxation processes
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: The behavior of particles subject to a nonlinear drag force in a medium (nonlinear Brownian motion) is usually treated by means of the Fokker-Planck equation proposed by Klimontovich [Phys. Usp. 37, 737 (1994)]. However, the derivation of such an equation appears to be questionable since it involves unproved assumptions and does not take into account any relation between the assumptions and approximations leading (in kinetic theory) to a velocity-dependent friction coefficient and those necessary to obtain an appropriate kinetic equation. In spite of this, as far as we know, the limits of validity of the said equation have not yet been investigated. Such circumstances pose the general problem: what is (if any) the appropriate (approximate) differential kinetic equation which is really compatible with the Langevin equation for nonlinear Brownian motions? To adequately solve this problem, previous papers dealing with the behavior of heavy particles in light gases are reexamined. The study leads to the final conclusions that (1) the heavy-particle speed dependence of the friction coefficient (and of the fluctuating force), in the Langevin equation, makes it very difficult to derive an appropriate Fokker-Planck equation for nonlinear Brownian motion, particularly in the most general three-dimensional case, and (2) the searched appropriate (approximate) differential kinetic equation for the heavy particles really exists and is the fourth-order equation following from the Boltzmann equation for a quasi-Rayleigh gas. Then it is shown that, on the contrary, the equation for the heavy-particle mean velocity relaxation following from the Fokker-Planck equation proposed by Klimontovich conflicts with that directly derived from the Langevin equation, a circumstance which now proves the inadequacy of the Klimontovich approach. Subsequently, some relaxation processes of particular interest are studied. So both the correct time-dependent mean velocity and the mean distance traveled by an anisotropic swarm of heavy particles are obtained, and the results are discussed assuming an interaction force between heavy- and gas-particles proportional to inverse powers of their mutual distance. Moreover, the correct relaxation equation for the heavy-particle mean-square speed is also achieved, and the difference with the corresponding result following from the Klimontovich theory is pointed out. An approximate method of solution of the said correct relaxation equation is also proposed. Finally, the limits of validity of the present theory are discussed.

apsDecisions.title: Expressivity of quantum graph neural networks with variable-dimension edge qudits
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: This work presents a quantum graph neural network architecture in which each edge of the input graph carries a d-level quantum system and the model acts on the associated line graph. The set of circuits generated by the model is dense in the unitary group of the total Hilbert space, subject to an irrationality condition on the angular parameters. The model constructively separates pairs of 1-WL-indistinguishable graphs whose line graphs are k-WL-distinguishable, making it a quantum model that lies beyond the 1-WL ceiling. The function class realizable at dimension d admits a strictly positive residual loss floor, which yields a criterion for adaptive expansion of the local dimension. Numerical validation confirms the impossibility of separation by node-based architectures for SRG(16,6,2,2), establishes the 3-WL distinguishability of its line graphs, and demonstrates direct separation by the edge-qudit architecture between the Petersen graph and the pentagonal prism. Taken together, these results establish the structural expressivity of edge qudits as an advantage over existing node-based architectures.

apsDecisions.title: Density-selected topological pathways in the melting of single-particle-thick stripes
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: The melting of stripe-forming systems involves changes in connectivity that are not fully captured by conventional structural and orientational descriptors. We investigate a two-dimensional model with competing interactions whose low-temperature phase consists of one-particle-thick stripes. Molecular dynamics simulations along seven heating isochores are analyzed using thermodynamic, orientational, dynamical, and graph-based observables. Heating produces a multistage reconstruction in which the loss of stripe alignment and the reorganization of filament connectivity occur over distinct temperature ranges. Density controls whether the disordered filaments fragment into finite polymerlike clusters or remain joined in a dynamically fluid, system-spanning network. The topological observables distinguish these outcomes, which are not resolved by the thermodynamic and orientational responses alone. Thus, the same ordered stripe microphase can melt into topologically distinct fluids selected by density.

apsDecisions.title: Impedance of an electric double layer capacitor with a multi-component electrolyte
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: I derive the impedance response of an ideal electrolyte containing an arbitrary number of mobile ionic species between blocking planar electrodes, described by the Poisson-Nernst-Planck equations. By transforming the linearized equations to a charge-salt description, the response is written in terms of a multi-component diffusion-migration matrix and its eigenvalues and eigenvectors. When all diffusivities are equal, the charge mode decouples from the neutral concentration subspace and the classical binary-electrolyte result is recovered. In contrast, unequal diffusivities couple charge relaxation to one or more neutral composition modes. For a ternary electrolyte with two cations and one anion, this coupling produces additional diffusive features and broadens the crossover between resistive and capacitive regimes. The results found in this paper provide a minimal continuum explanation for why mixed electrolytes can display impedance spectra that cannot be interpreted as a simple binary electrolyte with an averaged diffusion coefficient.

apsDecisions.title: Unique nonconcentric semicircular arrays of nanoparticles via controlled gravitational force
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: The dynamic behavior of the three-phase contact line (TPCL) during droplet evaporation plays a critical role in governing particle assembly processes, enabling spatially controlled deposition of nanomaterials at micro/nanoscales. This phenomenon utilizes evaporation-driven capillary and possible Marangoni flows arising from surface tension gradients to direct particle migration, resulting in pattern formation through TPCL pinning-depinning dynamics and solvent gradient effects. In this study, we report the formation of unique nonconcentric semicircular arrays of nanoparticle deposition on hydrophilic silicon substrates. This patterning is achieved by manipulating TPCL dynamics through gravity-induced asymmetric droplet deformation. A droplet placed on an inclined substrate adopts an asymmetric shape due to the competing effects of surface tension and gravity, producing spatially heterogeneous TPCL motion characterized by distinct pinning and depinning regimes. These events drive directional deposition of suspended particles, facilitating the self-organization of semicircular stripes. The physical features of the stripe patterns, such as density and spacing, are precisely tunable by adjusting the effective parallel gravitational force (Fg∥), which we control via substrate inclination (α) and droplet volume (V). A universal linear relationship between stripe density and Fg∥ is found, independent of the mode of force modulation. However, subtle changes in the structural morphology of the surface pattern have been observed, resulting in periodic semicircular patterns with varying radii of curvature, while the final structure is significantly influenced by the sample preparation-related memory effect. An assembly mechanism and an empirical relation based on the experimental results are provided to correlate stripe density with α and V, capturing the interplay between gravitational forces and TPCL kinetics.

apsDecisions.title: Finite-size corrections to the crosscap overlap in the two-dimensional Ising model
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We analyze the finite-size corrections to the crosscap overlap in the two-dimensional classical Ising model along its self-dual critical line. Using a fermionic formulation, we express the lattice crosscap overlap in terms of Bogoliubov angles and develop a contour-integral approach by analytically continuing the lattice momentum to the complex plane. This leads to a remarkably simple expression for the crosscap overlap, which demonstrates that the finite-size corrections decay exponentially with system size. We further derive an exact analytical formula for the corresponding decay constant and show that it is determined by the complex singularity structure of the Bogoliubov angle.

apsDecisions.title: Boundary-driven anisotropic coarsening in conserved phase separation
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Universal scaling in phase separation is typically assumed to be isotropic in systems with conserved dynamics. Here we show that boundary forcing alone can break this dynamical scaling symmetry, leading to anisotropic coarsening, with different effective global growth laws observed parallel and perpendicular to the boundary. We consider a ternary mixture with two conserved components and a passive species undergoing surface evaporation, which provides a simple setting to investigate this effect. In this case, evaporation leads to a progressive mass loss and to the formation of macroscopic concentration gradients, which, in turn, drive anisotropic coarsening, with different effective growth laws observed parallel and perpendicular to the boundary. At the same time, bulk regions appear to retain the standard Model B scaling, suggesting that the observed anisotropy is mainly induced by boundary fluxes rather than by changes in the intrinsic dynamics. Our results indicate that boundary conditions can play an important role in breaking scaling symmetry and may offer a way to influence coarsening behavior in nonequilibrium phase separation.

apsDecisions.title: Experimental investigation of Lévy flights for step-length distributions with a length-dependent local power exponent
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Light propagating in a resonant atomic vapor performs a Lévy flight random walk, in which rare long steps dominate the transport. In contrast to the ideal power-law step-length distributions usually assumed in the literature, the actual distribution in atomic vapors is characterized by a local Lévy index α(ℓ) that varies smoothly with the step length ℓ. Moreover, the walker alternates between two distinct step-length distributions, depending on whether an atomic collision occurs during each scattering event. In this work, we experimentally investigate which effective Lévy index is retrieved from diffuse transmission measurements in such a nonideal Lévy flight, and how the alternation between the two distributions influences the transmission. From measurements in a dense cesium vapor for different system sizes and atomic densities, we show that the measured Lévy index corresponds to the local exponent evaluated at the system size, αT=α(ℓ=L). Surprisingly, the measured values are consistent with the step-length distribution associated with atomic collisions, that has heavier tails, even when the collision probability is small. Monte Carlo simulations of walkers alternating between two Lévy-like step-length distributions support the experimental findings. Our results extend the study of Lévy flights to a class of nonideal random walks, with length-dependent local exponents and alternating step-length distributions, that are likely to be relevant in other real physical systems.

apsDecisions.title: Persistence properties of a phase-ordering system with competing dynamics
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Understanding persistence properties of a system with respect to its underlying microscopic dynamics provides important insights into the associated first-passage behavior. Here, we investigate the persistence properties during phase ordering in the two-dimensional (d=2) Ising model evolving under competing nonconserved spin-flip and conserved spin-exchange dynamics by means of Monte Carlo simulations at zero temperature. We examine three distinct persistence probabilities: (i) the total persistence probability, defined as the probability that a lattice site has never experienced a change in the sign of the spin residing there; (ii) the spin-flip persistence probability, which exclusively measures the fraction of sites that have never undergone a spin-flip event; and (iii) the composite persistence probability, defined as the fraction of sites that have experienced neither a spin-flip nor a spin-exchange event. In the asymptotic regime, both the total and spin-flip persistence probabilities exhibit identical power-law decay, irrespective of the relative occurrence probability of the spin-flip move pr. The corresponding persistence exponent θi≈0.225, is found to be consistent with the value reported for systems evolving purely under nonconserved dynamics. We further demonstrate that both persistence measures satisfy the scaling relation d−dfi=θi/αi, where dfi is the fractal dimension of the corresponding persistence lattice and αi≈1/2 characterizes the asymptotic power-law growth of spatially correlated regions of nonpersistent spins. In contrast, although the composite persistence probability also exhibits asymptotic power-law decay, the corresponding persistence exponent θc and fractal dimension dfc of the persistence lattice show strong dependence on pr. Combined with the presence of a universal growth exponent αc≈1/2, this leads to the breakdown of the scaling relation among the characteristic exponents for the composite persistence.

apsDecisions.title: Using echo-state networks to reproduce rare events in chaotic systems
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Echo-state networks (ESNs) are known to reproduce the trajectories and main properties of chaotic attractors. Here, we investigate the question of whether ESNs can reproduce rare events in a system with a stationary distribution with slowly decaying bounded tails. In particular, we consider the chaotic four-dimensional competitive Lotka-Volterra system, and quantify extremes using the generalized extreme value distribution. In stationary simulations, the ESN reproduces the stationary distributions and rare event statistics with high accuracy. In addition, the ESN also reproduces rare event statistics for nonequilibrium ensemble simulations for initial conditions relatively close to the underlying attractor. However, the performance of the ESN deteriorates as the ensemble spread increases and trajectories explore regions of phase space not represented in the training data.

apsDecisions.title: Delay-controlled heterogeneous nucleation in adaptive dynamical networks
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Phase transitions constitute fundamental mechanisms underlying abrupt or qualitative changes in the collective dynamics of interacting units across a wide range of natural and engineered systems. In dynamical networks, such transitions lead to significant reorganization in the coordinated behavior of coupled elements. In adaptive dynamical networks, the connectivity evolves dynamically in response to the states of the nodes, resulting in a coevolution of the structure and dynamics. In this work, we report two distinct forms of heterogeneous nucleation that give rise to single-step and multistep phase transitions toward global synchronization in finite-size adaptive networks with connection delays. We demonstrate that the nature of the nucleation transition is governed by both the presence and magnitude of the delay, as well as the class of natural frequency distribution. Using a collective coordinate framework, we develop a mean-field description of cluster dynamics and derive an analytical upper bound condition for the existence of two-cluster states, which shows excellent agreement with numerical simulations. Furthermore, we extend the analysis to systems with distributed delays and obtain corresponding analytical conditions. Our results provide a theoretical framework for understanding synchronization transitions in adaptive networks with time-delayed interactions.

apsDecisions.title: Sandpile models on complex networks
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We investigate the sandpile model on complex networks by developing a branching-process framework that explicitly incorporates dissipation during avalanche propagation. Unlike classical branching descriptions, which assume conservative transport and locally treelike independence, the present approach introduces grain-loss effects directly into the offspring distribution, yielding generalized generating functions for dissipative avalanche dynamics. In the dissipative regime, avalanche-size distributions acquire exponential cutoffs while preserving topology-dependent scaling behavior. Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical predictions on sparse random networks and reveal systematic deviations in highly structured topologies. In particular, using Holme-Kim clustered scale-free networks, we show that the avalanche exponent is relatively insensitive to weak-to-moderate clustering but decreases substantially in the strongly clustered regime, especially as the triangle-closing probability approaches unity. This decrease is accompanied by an enhanced probability of large cascades, showing that sufficiently abundant short cycles generate strong correlations that challenge the classical independent-branch approximation. Surprisingly, trees also exhibit substantial deviations from a power law because low edge density and the abundance of leaves constrain avalanche propagation. These results show that dissipation, clustering, and sparse connectivity fundamentally reshape the avalanche size distribution of the sandpile model on networks and establish quantitative limits for branching-process descriptions of avalanche dynamics.

apsDecisions.title: Evolutionary hysteresis: Cycling about in a rugged landscape
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 统计物理、软物质、复杂网络或连续介质主题；未见目标晶体电子材料新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: In this work, we integrate theoretical modeling, molecular simulation, and empirical analysis to identify and characterize evolutionary hysteresis. We first show how epistatic interactions create bistable fitness landscapes and structural hysteresis in a two-locus Wright-Fisher model, revealing two distinct hysteresis regimes under cyclic and noisy selection. Notably, an epistatically constrained population achieves maximal average fitness at an intermediate level of environmental stochasticity. We then extend this framework to more complex systems, demonstrating robust hysteresis loops in both a disordered multilocus model and in biophysically realistic simulations of protein structural flexibility. Finally, we present empirical evidence of evolutionary hysteresis. By analyzing two decades of metagenomic time-series data from freshwater C. Nanopelagicaceae experiencing strong seasonal temperature cycles, we find that approximately 63% of seasonally oscillating alleles exhibit nonzero loop area versus temperature, and a majority retain substantial area under any constant phase shift of temperature, inconsistent with a simple evolutionary lag. Together, our results establish hysteresis as a general, measurable feature of evolution with a potential for probing features of complex fitness landscapes.

apsDecisions.title: Bubble dynamics in a Hele-Shaw channel and velocity selection without surface tension
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 流体力学、湍流或流固耦合主题；非目标晶体/超导/磁性电子材料。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Inviscid bubble dynamics in a viscous fluid, moving with velocity V far from the bubble, is considered. The Cauchy problem of recovering the bubble evolution from its initial shape is completely solved without surface tension. This dynamical system is well-posed (after a Tikhonov regularization) and possesses an extensive list of unsteady nonsingular closed-form solutions due to integrability. A new rational class of solutions is obtained and added to the logarithmic class found earlier [Phys. Rev. E 89, 061003(R) (2014)]. The only attractor of the system selects the observable bubble shape and velocity U=2V from the continuum of possible solutions. The attractor is asymptotically stable. Numerical results essential for illustrating and understanding the most salient geometric aspects of the bubble dynamics are presented.

apsDecisions.title: Complex dynamical regimes of the Tayler-Spruit dynamo
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 流体力学、湍流或流固耦合主题；非目标晶体/超导/磁性电子材料。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Astrophysical dynamos feature various spatial structures and dynamical regimes, ranging from hemispherical magnetic fields to the random reversals of the geodynamo. The Tayler-Spruit dynamo, recently confirmed in direct numerical simulations, has been invoked to explain angular momentum transport in stellar radiative zones and magnetar formation in a proto-neutron star spun up by fallback accretion. Whether this dynamo mechanism can lead to different dynamical regimes remains an open question. Using three-dimensional direct numerical simulations, we model the dynamics of a stably stratified spherical Couette flow, with the outer sphere rotating faster than the inner one. While the generation of strong stationary and hemispherical dynamos has been observed in our previous studies, we report the existence of reversals and complex temporal dynamics. We observe that the dynamics is strongly correlated with the equatorial symmetry breaking of the flow. Focusing on a fiducial dynamo simulation, we propose an interpretation of its dynamics that consists of the coupling of two large-scale magnetic modes with opposite equatorial symmetries by the flow symmetry breaking. While this interpretation captures the simplest observed dynamics, the nonlinear interaction between a higher number of magnetic modes is certainly required to describe more complex regimes. The wide diversity of dynamical regimes generated by the Tayler-Spruit dynamo may have interesting implications for the geometry of the neutron star magnetic fields, and therefore neutron star emissions.

apsDecisions.title: Dynamic mode decomposition using standard particle image velocimetry data
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 流体力学、湍流或流固耦合主题；非目标晶体/超导/磁性电子材料。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) is a widely used technique for analyzing flow dynamics, particularly with experimental data. Traditionally, in experimental applications, the method frequently relies on time-resolved particle image velocimetry (PIV) data to construct an embedding to track incremental changes in the flow state. In this study, we propose an extension of DMD to enable the extraction of DMD modes from standard (non-time-resolved) PIV data. Standard PIV data typically consist of paired snapshots of particle positions taken with a small time delay, used to compute instantaneous velocity fields. However, the time delay between successive pairs is often too large to effectively capture the evolution of the velocity field. To address this limitation, we associate particle-position data with flow dynamics by introducing a gap-based DMD (gDMD) formulation. In this approach, the local distribution of seed particles is mapped to directional gap fields, which are then used as observables for extracting velocity-associated DMD modes. The method is showcased using two direct numerical simulation databases: a confined two-dimensional cylinder wake and the fluidic pinball configuration, together with PIV data of a rectangular jet. In the numerical case, artificial PIV data were generated by seeding the flow with passive tracers. Our results indicate that dominant DMD modes can be accurately predicted even with significant time delays between successive snapshot pairs—an interval that would typically hinder the application of standard DMD. This approach broadens the applicability of DMD, providing a robust tool for analyzing flow dynamics with non-time-resolved PIV data.

apsDecisions.title: Crystallography of periodic nanotextures in a strained Mott insulator

detailFetch.abstract: Here we investigate stripes of alternating structural phases spontaneously forming in epitaxially strained Ca2RuO4 thin films below the metal-insulator transition. Using large-volume X-ray reciprocal-space mapping, we show that satellite-pattern intensities across 49 different Bragg reflections collapse onto a single parameter-free curve. The collapse identifies a coherent martensitic laminate of few-nm wide domains separated by {012} interfaces, with displacements along [021]. Satellite-extinction analysis demonstrates that both coexisting phases retain the bulk orthorhombic space group despite the pseudocubic LaAlO3 substrate, biaxial epitaxial strain, and intrinsic strain at the interfaces. Classical invariant-plane-strain crystallography thus governs the nanoscale domain geometry of a Mott insulator with intertwined magnetic, electronic, and lattice order.

apsDecisions.title: Magnetic-field-free quantum interference and universal Josephson diode effect driven by superfluid momentum

detailFetch.abstract: Josephson quantum interference has hitherto been tethered to magnetic fields. Moreover, the Josephson diode effect (JDE) is often deemed anomalous and tied to broken symmetries in exotic phases. In planar Josephson junctions made with B i 2 O 2 S e and bilayer graphene, we show that the JDE is a natural extension of the Josephson effect achievable through a universal mechanism. We replace magnetic fields with current-induced superfluid momentum generated in high-kinetic-inductance superconducting leads. This enables all-electric quantum interference and provides a magnetic-free, phase-sensitive probe for novel materials with unconventional superconductivity.

apsDecisions.title: Sb-5 p -mediated antiparallel Nd-Fe coupling in ${\rm Nd_3Fe_3Sb_7}$

detailFetch.abstract: We uncover the microscopic mechanism underlying the antiparallel Nd–Fe coupling in the intermetallic 4 f –3 d –5 p compound Nd 3 Fe 3 Sb 7 by means of high-field x-ray magnetic circular dichroism (XMCD) spectroscopy, complemented by magnetization measurements and density-functional-theory (DFT) calculations. This coupling is unexpected for intermetallics composed of light rare-earth and transition-metal elements. Sb M 4 , 5 -edge XMCD measurements indicate a clear spin polarization of Sb 5 p states antiparallel to the Fe 3 d moments. DFT calculations reveal the site-dependent character of the Sb moments and, together with the Fe–Sb antiparallel alignment seen by XMCD, identify a Fe 3 d –Sb 5 p –Nd 5 d hybridization pathway for the antiparallel Nd–Fe coupling. Pulsed-field XMCD reveals a field-induced spin reorientation through the evolution of the c -axis projections of the Nd and Fe moments. Nd 3 Fe 3 Sb 7 , thus, provides a platform for exploring antiparallel rare-earth–transition-metal ( R – T ) coupling mediated by transition-metal 3 d –ligand p –rare-earth 5 d hybridization in light- R – T intermetallics with p -elements.

apsDecisions.title: Polarization rotation-driven spin-topological transition in ferroelectric bismuth monolayer

detailFetch.abstract: Bismuth monolayer is the first two-dimensional elemental ferroelectric and an appealing platform for coupling polar order to spin-orbit-driven topology. However, its microscopic switching mechanism remains elusive. Here, using first-principles lattice dynamics and symmetry-adapted mode analysis, we identify a previously overlooked rotational pathway for in-plane polarization switching. Its energy barrier is more than four times lower than that of direct reversal, naturally explaining the vortexlike domain textures observed in molecular dynamics simulations. Remarkably, this polarization rotation also drives a spin-topological transition, changing the spin Chern number from C s = − 2 to 0 . Directional uniaxial strain further steers the polarization orientation and tunes the associated topological transition. These results establish polarization rotation as a feasible switching mechanism of ferroelectric Bi monolayer and as an efficient route to electrically and mechanically programmable topology in two-dimensional ferroelectrics.

apsDecisions.title: Stochastic resonance in disordered charge-density-wave systems

detailFetch.abstract: Ultrafast disordering observed after photo-excitation challenges the conventional picture of photo- induced transitions where symmetry-breaking takes place along a single collective coordinate. We propose that key spectroscopic signatures of these transient disordered states can be revealed through stochastic resonance, a hallmark of nonlinear stochastic dynamics. Studying the disordered phase of Holstein model we show that, at given frequency, the linear response as a function of temperature has a peak, which indicates enhanced coherent switching between metastable configurations. From this resonance, we extract the intrinsic stochastic transition timescale and energy barrier separating equivalent local minima. This mechanism offers a new perspective to identify and characterize hidden disordered phases in driven many-body systems.

apsDecisions.title: Kineoelasticity and nonreciprocal phonons by Rashba-induced interfacial spin-lattice coupling

detailFetch.abstract: We identify a previously unrecognized spin-lattice coupling allowed by broken inversion symmetry that can be viewed as a lattice analogue of electronic Rashba spin-orbit coupling. In the low-frequency regime, where magnons are integrated out, its interplay with the conventional magnetoelastic coupling generates a kineo-elastic term that couples strain and lattice velocity, giving rise to nonreciprocal phonon velocity. We further analyze the full magnon-phonon spectrum and find that the competition between interfacial spin-lattice and magnetoelastic couplings leads to directional hybridization and absorption, yielding asymmetric phonon propagation lengths for opposite directions. Our results indicate that such interfacial spin-lattice coupling can provide an efficient route to nonreciprocal phonon propagation in magnetic heterostructures with strong Rashba spin–orbit coupling.

apsDecisions.title: Excitonic-superconducting coexistence and emergent nematic superconductivity driven by spontaneous symmetry breaking

detailFetch.abstract: Excitonic insulating (EI) and superconducting (SC) orders are generally regarded as mutually exclusive electronic instabilities. Within a self-consistent microscopic theory, we study electronic systems hosting an EI phase in the presence of SC pairing and show that an intrinsic mismatch between electron and hole Fermi surfaces fundamentally reshapes this competition. This mismatch stabilizes FFLO-like electron-hole pairing and drives spontaneous symmetry breaking of the EI state. The resulting symmetry breaking reconstructs the pairing phase space for SC and EI state, such that different regions of the Fermi surface complementarily support either EI or SC correlations, leading to a natural coexistence of the two orders. Notably, the emergent SC state consequently breaks rotational symmetry and develops intrinsic nematic superconductivity, even in the absence of explicit symmetry-breaking fields (such as magnetic fields, spin-orbit coupling, or bare band-structure anisotropy). Our results suggest that candidate materials such as monolayer 1T ′ -MoTe 2 and the square-net semimetal NaAlSi may provide promising platforms for observing this phenomenon. More broadly, these findings reveal a unique mechanism by which competing many-body orders generate electronic nematicity, suggesting a broader route toward spontaneous anisotropic electronic states in correlated quantum materials.

apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We propose a quantum-battery charger based on a driven bosonic Kitaev chain (BKC), where chiral squeezing converts passive input fluctuations into ordered, nonpassive battery states. While a coherent input pulse exhibits phase-sensitive chiral transport, the charging dynamics is dominated by bidirectionally propagating fluctuations that are amplified and squeezed into orthogonal quadratures at opposite chain ends. In contrast to conventional phase-preserving amplifiers, our scheme stores largely extractable energy and achieves a worklike signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) near unity, even in the presence of thermal noise and moderate symmetry-preserving disorder.

apsDecisions.title: Superconducting Qutrit Link beyond the Qubit Limit
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 涉及凝聚态/材料相关关键词，但尚未确证直接实验生长或目标物性的新证据；保留候补，不能仅据标题称已排除。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Superconducting microwave links have enabled deterministic state transfer and remote entanglement between qubits, but deterministic links have so far operated with an effectively two-dimensional transmitted Hilbert space. Here we demonstrate a superconducting qutrit link between two independently packaged nodes connected by a microwave channel. Each node combines a transmon qutrit, a transmission resonator, and a tunable Purcell-filter interface, allowing the two remote microwave-photon interfaces to be matched in both frequency and bandwidth. We implement two transition-selective photon-mediated operations that transfer the |e⟩ and |f⟩ qutrit components in distinct temporal modes of the same channel. We tomographically characterize arbitrary qutrit-state transfer, obtaining a mean transferred-state fidelity of 83.68% and a qutrit process fidelity of 77.12%, exceeding both the classical qutrit-transfer benchmark and the best possible average fidelity of an effective qubit channel used to transmit an arbitrary qutrit. Using partial-transfer operations, we reconstruct a remote two-qutrit state with negativity 0.730, a tomography-inferred dense-coding capacity of 2.273 bits, and a tomography-inferred Collins-Gisin-Linden-Massar-Popescu (CGLMP) parameter I3=2.332, all beyond the corresponding qubit or local bounds. These results demonstrate a superconducting microwave link that uses the native three-level structure of transmons as a genuine high-dimensional communication resource.

apsDecisions.title: Probing Extragalactic Ultralight Axion Dark Matter with Decade-Long Blazar Optical Polarimetry of 1ES 1959 + 650
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Axions or axion-like particles (ALPs) are well-motivated dark matter (DM) candidates whose coupling to photons induces periodic oscillations in the polarization angle of astrophysical light. This Letter reports the first search for such a signature using 10 years of optical polarimetric monitoring of the blazar 1ES 1959+650. No statistically significant periodicity is detected, determined by a Lomb-Scargle periodogram combined with Monte Carlo analysis. Assuming a central DM density in the host galaxy, this null result places tight upper limits on the ALP-photon coupling constant at gaγ<(1.3×10−13−6.0×10−10)GeV−1 across a broad ALP mass range of ma∼(1.4×10−23−5.2×10−20)  eV. Assuming a soliton-core DM density, we obtain upper limits of gaγ<(2.5×10−13−6.2×10−13)GeV−1 over the same ALP mass range. Our constraints surpass those from Very Long Baseline Array polarimetry of active galactic jets and from polarimetric data of the European Pulsar Timing Array, and are competitive with those from long-term Galactic pulsar timing of PSR J0437-4715 over the same ALP mass window. These results establish long-term blazar polarimetry as a competitive and complementary approach for probing axion-like DM on extragalactic scales.

apsDecisions.title: Precision Isotope-Shift Measurement of the S 1 0 ↔ P 3 2 Transition and a Multitransition King-Plot Consistency Test
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We present precision spectroscopy and isotope shift measurement of the S10↔P32 clock transition in neutral ytterbium (Yb) atoms. By revealing a magic wavelength at 905.4(2) nm, we successfully achieve the atomic spectrum narrower than 100 Hz. The interleaved clock operation between isotopes allows us to determine isotope shifts of four bosonic isotope pairs at Hz-level uncertainties, which is combined with those of other four ultranarrow transitions in Yb and Yb+ to construct the King plot. We show that a rich dataset spanning multiple transitions enables a test of a restricted isotope-shift ansatz comprising the leading mass and field shifts, one effective factorized higher-order standard model contribution, and a new-particle contribution. Within this ansatz, the five-transition data are inconsistent with the new-particle contribution serving as the sole additional contribution over the mass ranges mϕ≤6.5  keV and 18  keV≤mϕ<100  keV, while the previous works rely on another bound set by the neutron scattering and (g−2)e measurements. This Letter paves the way for the effective use of precision isotope shift data in the King plot analysis and stimulates further measurements in Yb and other elements.

apsDecisions.title: Experimental Subdiffraction Source Discrimination Enabled by Spatial Demultiplexing and Single-Photon Detectors
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We experimentally demonstrate a universal, parameter-independent test for asymmetric source discrimination below the diffraction limit. The test exploits spatial-mode demultiplexing (SPADE) and single-photon detection to discriminate the presence of a faint source in the vicinity of a brighter one. We develop a complete theory of the test in the presence of arbitrary modal crosstalk and show that the crosstalk-affected test retains a favorable error exponent over diffraction-limited direct imaging, provided that the crosstalk remains below a threshold Cmax≃1/9. This establishes a quantitative condition under which the subdiffraction advantage of SPADE survives realistic imperfections. We experimentally test the scheme for a range of source separations and intensity ratios, without requiring prior knowledge of these parameters. The measured false-negative error rates are in good agreement with the theoretical model and systematically outperform direct imaging. These results demonstrate that SPADE provides a robust and experimentally accessible advantage for asymmetric subdiffraction hypothesis testing in the photon-starved regime, even in the presence of realistic modal crosstalk.

apsDecisions.title: Bridging Marcus–Landauer Transport Regimes in Orbital-Gated Molecular Junctions
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 涉及凝聚态/材料相关关键词，但尚未确证直接实验生长或目标物性的新证据；保留候补，不能仅据标题称已排除。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Charge transport in molecular junctions is commonly described by either Marcus theory, which captures thermally activated hopping via redox processes, or Landauer formalism, which models elastic tunneling between two electrodes. However, real molecular junctions often operate in an intermediate regime between the two transport limits, requiring a comprehensive understanding. Here, we investigate orbital-gated molecular transistors fabricated by forming self-assembled monolayers of redox-active ferrocene-terminated alkanethiols on an Au bottom electrode, contacting them with a graphene top electrode and gating them through ionic media. By tuning the gate voltage to modulate the energetic alignment of the frontier molecular orbital, we observed a continuous variation of the activation energy from 3.8 to 117.8 meV. We find that the dominant transport type can be switched between Marcus-type (thermally activated) and Landauer-type (temperature-independent) behavior, as the orbital enters or exits the transmission window defined by the electrochemical potentials of the electrodes. This crossover under orbital gating is quantitatively described by the multispace density functional theory and the lifetime-broadened Marcus theory. Our orbital-gated molecular transistors bridge the hopping–tunneling transport regimes, providing a device-scale platform for controlling the dominant transport phenomena.

apsDecisions.title: Projected Coherent Perfect Absorption at Exceptional Points via Nonlocal Elastodynamic Coupling
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 涉及凝聚态/材料相关关键词，但尚未确证直接实验生长或目标物性的新证据；保留候补，不能仅据标题称已排除。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: In non-Hermitian physics, coherent perfect absorption at an exceptional point (CPA EP) emerges as a unique degenerate state that can manifest anomalously broadened absorption line shape implying strong robustness, which apparently contradicts the extreme sensitivity rooted in EPs. To investigate this unique state, we design an underwater acoustic metasurface comprising a beam splitter and a retroreflector on opposite sides. We leverage fluid-solid interaction (FSI) as a powerful mechanism to engineer the non-Hermitian coupling, circumventing the necessity for difficult-to-tune gain or loss for the degeneracy. FSI-induced strong nonlocal elastodynamic coupling concurrently morphs the previously independent spatial subspaces, creating contrasting non-Hermitian behaviors in the respective subspaces, with one encoding the projected CPA EP. We prove that the CPA EP inherits core attributes from both states, manifesting the coexistence of macroscopic operational robustness (from CPA) and microscopic topological hypersensitivity (from EP). We further experimentally demonstrate that the CPA EP, in turn, acts as a knob to modulate the FSI coupling channel, allowing its full activation (for perfect anomalous deflection) or, by leveraging the missing dimension, complete suppression (for total reflection). This synergy between FSI and non-Hermitian degeneracies shows potential for multifunctional hydroacoustic devices.

apsDecisions.title: Brewster-Anomaly Delocalization for Free-Electron Radiation
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 涉及凝聚态/材料相关关键词，但尚未确证直接实验生长或目标物性的新证据；保留候补，不能仅据标题称已排除。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Localization effects are central to disordered electronics and photonics. In electronics, Anderson localization governs electron confinement in randomly perturbed lattices. Similarly, its photonic counterpart inhibits light transport via disorder but with a unique exception: Brewster-anomaly delocalization, where the Brewster effect prevents multiple-scattering interference and counteracts the localization. Despite extensive research in electronics and photonics separately, the intricate role of localization effects in interactions between free electrons and light—vital for lasers, accelerators, microscopy and spectroscopy, and quantum information—remains largely unexplored. At the same time, localization effects are widely regarded as a key factor limiting the efficient coupling between free electrons and light in random media. Here, we overcome this key limitation via the unconventional interplay between Brewster-anomaly delocalization and free-electron radiation. In this way, free-electron radiation can be localization-free, intense and directional even in strongly disordered, unengineered multilayers. Essentially, this delocalization-mediated free-electron radiation is remarkably invariant not only to the random-medium configuration, but also to the light frequency and the electron velocity. Our findings unlock new opportunities for particle detectors and achromatic light sources operating in easy-to-fabricate complex media at previously inaccessible frequencies.

apsDecisions.title: Chiral Casimir-Polder Force from Chiral Anomaly in Weyl Semimetals
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 涉及凝聚态/材料相关关键词，但尚未确证直接实验生长或目标物性的新证据；保留候补，不能仅据标题称已排除。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We propose a novel chiral-discriminatory Casimir-Polder interaction between chiral molecules and Weyl semimetals, originating from the chiral anomaly. This interaction is uniquely governed by the molecule’s electric dipole moment, enabling chiral discrimination even when the optical rotatory strength of the molecule vanishes. For the chiral molecule C20H16ClNOS (characterized by strong spin-orbit coupling) and a rationally tailored Weyl semimetal, first-principles calculations predict a significantly enhanced chiral-discriminatory Casimir-Polder force compared to interactions between chiral molecule dimethyl disulphide and chiral metamaterial. We further propose a Stern-Gerlach-type spatial deflection measurement to isolate this chiral-specific interaction.

apsDecisions.title: Compositional Proofreading through Critical Self-Tuning
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 涉及凝聚态/材料相关关键词，但尚未确证直接实验生长或目标物性的新证据；保留候补，不能仅据标题称已排除。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: High-dimensional multicomponent systems, including immune and epigenetic repertoires, must selectively retain rare, beneficial components while purging a large influx of suboptimal variants. I demonstrate that critical tuning of component control parameters through competition naturally implements proofreading in these systems. Competition for shared inputs pins the system to the marginal stability threshold of the most persistent species. This grants that species an extended lifetime and concentrates a macroscopic fraction of the population in that species, while forcing less-stable variants into rapid drift-driven turnover. When the aggregate drive exceeds a critical influx, pinning fails and all components enter a rapid-turnover regime. Applying this framework to biological memory, I identify the hallmarks of this effect in plasma cell accumulation dynamics and propose that altered pinning dynamics may represent failure points across biological domains, including cancer, immunodeficiencies, and the aberrant activation of harmful genomic elements during aging.

apsDecisions.title: Bidirectional Teleportation Using Scrambling Dynamics: A Practical Protocol
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We show that quantum information scrambling can enable a generic swap gate between collective degrees of freedom in systems without universal local control. Our protocol combines a Hayden-Preskill type recovery scheme, associated with the black hole information paradox, with quantum teleportation and runs them in parallel and in opposite directions, enabling bidirectional exchange of quantum states through global interactions alone. This approach cleanly distinguishes the roles of information spreading, entanglement, and chaos for enabling both coherent state transfer and recovery. We propose an experimental realization using the Dicke model, which can be realized in optical cavity and trapped-ion platforms, highlighting the utility of holography in designing practical quantum gates.

apsDecisions.title: Local Obstructions to Trapped-Region Escape in Modified Gravity
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Energy conditions in modified gravity are commonly imposed on an “effective” stress tensor that mixes physical matter with additional gravitational degrees of freedom, obscuring which sector actually controls null focusing, horizon multiplicity, and the disappearance of trapped regions. We develop a geometry-first alternative in spherical symmetry. For a normalized pair of future-directed radial null vectors, two longitudinal Ricci projections and one independent transverse Einstein projection obey exact area-weighted transport laws. These imply a trapping-persistence theorem: after a nondegenerate future-outer marginal sphere, a regular ingoing generator cannot exit the trapped region while the ingoing longitudinal and transverse convergence channels remain nonnegative. In metric f(R) gravity, with F≡df/dR>0, we then construct an entropy-resolved hierarchy based on the local Wald-density variable Fr2. In the longitudinal entropy-focusing law, the scalaron second derivative cancels exactly, leaving a nonpositive scalar-gradient square together with the physical matter projection; in the independent transverse entropy-transport law, all scalaron derivative terms cancel. Entropy trapping is consequently governed by the physical matter condition Tnn≥0 and an algebraic mixed threshold rather than by a fictitious effective fluid. The resulting hierarchy cleanly separates matter positivity, geometric focusing, marginal-surface recovery, and gravitational-entropy evolution, and identifies the precise local reversals required for regular inner horizons, throats, and trapped-to-antitrapped transitions.

apsDecisions.title: Beyond the Dilute Instanton Gas: Resurgence with Exact Saddles in the Double Well
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: The path-integral approach to the double well has long been limited by the dilute instanton gas approximation. We show that if the finite Euclidean-time structure is taken seriously by using exact saddles, the dilute gas can be sidestepped, allowing the partition function and energy levels to be computed systematically. At each instanton order, the full resurgent structure—which saddles contribute, what asymptotic growth is expected, and how ambiguities cancel—is encoded in a finite-dimensional Picard-Lefschetz contour integral over the quasizero modes with a clear geometric interpretation. Working at finite T is essential: the dilute instanton gas can only access the ground-state splitting, whereas the exact finite-T computation systematically produces the nonperturbative energy splittings for all excited states, including their full dependence on the level number. The key ingredients—Weierstrass elliptic functions for the saddles, Lamé operators for the fluctuations, and Picard-Fuchs equations for the periods—form a coherent mathematical framework that both overlaps and complements that of exact WKB.

apsDecisions.title: O(4)-Breaking Bubble
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: False vacuum decay in scalar field theory is thought to be dominated by Coleman’s O(4)-symmetric bounce, the minimum action nontrivial solution of the imaginary-time equations of motion. Beyond the bounce, nonconstructive existence proofs of O(4)-breaking solutions are available in the mathematics literature, but the solutions themselves, and their physics, have remained unknown. Considering the simple, bounded-below, scalar field potential V(ϕ)=(m2/2)ϕ2−(λ/4)ϕ4+(g/6)ϕ6, we construct a nonradial solution explicitly: two bubble tubes of opposite sign wrapping orthogonal rings, invariant under O(2)×O(2) rotations combined with a Z2 symmetry that exchanges the rings. The solution admits valid Cauchy data for real-time evolution from a t=0 slice, and supports an odd >1 number of unstable deformation modes. Having found this first solution we proceed to discover additional examples, in 3D as well as other 4D theories, including a Z2-violating potential and scalar QED for which there were no previously known existence proofs or O(4)-dominance theorems.

apsDecisions.title: Available Energy and Ground States of Convective Hydrodynamic and Hydromagnetic Instabilities
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: We propose a method for predicting the nonlinear extent of convective instabilities in neutral and magnetized fluids. The method extends Gardner’s restacking algorithm, which computes the available energy and ground states of collisionless plasmas in phase space, and combines it with Lagrangian relaxation, where fluid elements find lower-energy equilibria while preserving local invariants. For the incompressible Rayleigh-Taylor instability, the problem is equivalent to Gardner’s formulation and the restacking algorithm directly applies in configuration space. To treat compressibility in a general setting, we follow restacking with Lagrangian relaxation to obtain the ground state, and the results show excellent agreement with direct numerical simulations. Successful extension to the m=0 interchange instability in a Z pinch demonstrates the method’s potential as a general framework for estimating the nonlinear extent of convective instabilities, which can facilitate the design and operation of fusion reactors.

apsDecisions.title: Spontaneous Parity Breaking in Quantum Antiferromagnets on the Triangular Lattice
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 涉及凝聚态/材料相关关键词，但尚未确证直接实验生长或目标物性的新证据；保留候补，不能仅据标题称已排除。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Frustration on the triangular lattice has long been a source of intriguing and often debated phases in many-body systems. Although symmetry analysis has been employed, the role of the seemingly trivial parity symmetry has received little attention. In the work described in this Letter, we show that phases induced by frustration are systematically shaped by an implicit rule of thumb associated with spontaneous parity breaking in a weak longitudinal field. This principle enables us to anticipate and rationalize the regimes and conditions under which nontrivial phases emerge. For the spin-S antiferromagnetic XXZ model, we demonstrate that a controversial parity-broken phase appears at intermediate values of S. In bilayer systems, enhanced frustration leads to additional phases, such as supersolids, whose properties can be classified by their characteristic parity features. Benefiting from our improved tensor network contraction techniques, we confirm these results through large-scale tensor-network calculations. This study offers an alternative viewpoint and a systematic approach for examining the interplay between spin, symmetry, and frustration in many-body systems.

apsDecisions.title: Excitonic Stark Response Induced by Quantum Capacitance in van der Waals Heterostructures
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 范德华异质结的量子电容激子Stark响应；二维材料候选，需正文确认样品和实验路径。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Precise electrostatic control in van der Waals heterostructures is commonly described by a geometric capacitor model, which assumes that the internal electric field is fully determined by external gate voltages. Here, we show that this description breaks down in the presence of interfacial charge transfer, where quantum capacitance modifies the internal electrostatics. Using interlayer excitons as local probes, we observe a dipole-dependent energy splitting that persists even when the gate-induced geometric field is nominally canceled. This splitting reflects incomplete cancellation between gate- and carrier-induced fields set by quantum capacitance, while many-body renormalization is largely symmetric with respect to the two opposite dipole orientations, allowing the splitting to provide a direct optical measure of the local chemical potential. Our results reveal the central role of quantum capacitance in interface electrostatics and provide a route to probe it in operando.

apsDecisions.title: Escape from Heterogeneous Diffusion
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Many physical processes depend on the time it takes a diffusing particle to find a target. Though this classical quantity is now well understood in various scenarios, little is known when the diffusivity depends on the location of the particle. For such heterogeneous diffusion, the multiplicative noise requires an interpretation (e.g., Itô, Stratonovich, or kinetic). Here, we analytically determine the mean escape time and splitting probabilities for an arbitrary heterogeneous diffusion in an arbitrary three-dimensional domain with small targets that can be perfectly or imperfectly absorbing. Our analysis reveals general principles for how search depends on heterogeneous diffusion and its interpretation. An intricate picture emerges in which, for instance, increasing the diffusivity can decrease, have no effect, or even increase the escape time. Our results could be used to determine the appropriate interpretation for specific physical systems.

apsDecisions.title: Deep Thermalization and Measurements of Quantum Resources
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Quantum resource theories provide a unified framework for characterizing useful quantum phenomena subject to physical constraints, but are notoriously hard to assess in experimental systems. In this Letter, we introduce a unified protocol for quantifying the resource-generating power of arbitrary quantum evolutions applicable to multiple resource theories. It is based on deep thermalization, which has recently gained attention for its role in the emergence of quantum state designs from partial projective measurements. Central to our approach is the use of projected ensembles, recently employed to probe deep thermalization, together with new twirling identities that allow us to directly infer the resource-generating powers of the underlying dynamics. These identities further reveal how resources build up and thermalize in generic quantum circuits. Finally, we show that quantum resources themselves undergo deep thermalization at the subsystem level, offering a complementary and another experimentally accessible route to infer the resource-generating powers. Our Letter connects deep thermalization to resource quantification, offering a new perspective on the essential role of various resources in generating state designs and on efficient estimation of quantum resources in experiment.

apsDecisions.title: Spreading of Magic Resource under Unitary Clifford Dynamics
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本条主题为光学/器件/计算或其他应用；当前摘要或明确标题未给目标晶体、超导、重费米子、磁拓扑或二维电子材料的新实验。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Nonstabilizerness, or quantum magic resource, presents a valuable resource in quantum error correction and computation. We study the dynamics of locally injected nonstabilizerness in unitary Clifford circuits, where the total nonstabilizerness is conserved. However, the absence of physical observables quantifying nonstabilizerness precludes a direct microscopic or hydrodynamic description of its local distribution and dynamics. Using insights from stabilizer quantum error correcting codes, we rigorously show that the spatial distribution of nonstabilizerness can be inferred from a canonical representation of low-magic states, dubbed the bipartite magic gauge. Moreover, we propose two operationally relevant magic length scales. We numerically establish that, at early times, both length scales grow ballistically at distinct velocities set by the entanglement velocity, after which nonstabilizerness delocalizes. Our Letter sheds light on the spatiotemporal structure of quantum resources and complexity in many-body dynamics, opening up avenues for investigating their transport properties and further connections with quantum error correction.

apsDecisions.title: Identifying contributions to the superconducting diode effect through nonreciprocal superconducting properties

detailFetch.abstract: Nonreciprocal superconducting responses provide a sensitive probe of superconducting states in systems where inversion and time-reversal symmetries are broken. However, in the superconducting diode effect (SDE), where the critical current differs for opposite current directions, nonreciprocity can also arise from vortex-induced contributions caused by minute magnetic field misalignment, complicating its interpretation. Here, we investigate a noncentrosymmetric superlattice and demonstrate nonreciprocity in all three fundamental superconducting properties: the critical current, critical field, and superconducting transition temperature. By measuring the angular dependence of the nonreciprocal critical field $\Delta B_{\rmc 2}$ , we separate the contribution of misalignment-induced out-of-plane vortices from the in-plane response. We identify a sharply enhanced SDE emerging near $B_{\rmc 2}$ , accompanied by nonreciprocal responses in $T_{\rmc}$ . These observations exhibit phenomenology similar to that reported in layered superconductors, where an orbital-FFLO state with finite-momentum Cooper pairing has been reported. Our results establish a protocol for assessing out-of-plane vortex contributions to the superconducting diode effect and demonstrate that nonreciprocal responses provide complementary probes of unconventional superconducting states.

apsDecisions.title: Site-selective substitutions and magnetic structures in (Fe,Co) 2 (P,Si) compounds probed by x-ray linear dichroism and neutron diffraction

detailFetch.abstract: We investigate the crystallographic site occupancies and magnetic structures of Fe1.93-xCoxP1-ySiy 0 ≤ x ≤ 0.6 and 0 ≤ y ≤ 0.4 compounds using a combined x-ray absorption/linear dichroism (XAS/XLD) and neutron powder diffraction approach. Co K-edge XLD, supported by FDMNES simulations, provides direct spectroscopic evidence that Co preferentially occupies the tetrahedral 3f site of the hexagonal Fe2P-type structure. In contrast, P K-edge XLD and neutron diffraction show that Si is distributed over both 1b and 2c metalloid sites, with at most a weak preference for 2c, rather than the exclusive 2c occupation often assumed in calculations. Neutron diffraction further establishes that the hexagonal Fe2P-type compounds adopt a collinear ferromagnetic structure with ordered moments along the hexagonal c axis, whereas the orthorhombic Co2P-type phase observed at high Co content exhibits reduced and canted magnetic moments. Across the hexagonal series, Si substitution enhances the total magnetic moment through contributions from both 3f and 3g sites, whereas Co substitution suppresses it primarily via a reduction of the 3f site moment. These results provide an experimental basis for understanding why global structural parameters such as c/a alone are insufficient to rationalize the magnetic trends in (Fe,Co)2(P,Si), and demonstrate that site-selective occupancy must be included in structure-property relationships in Fe2P-derived hard-magnetic materials.

apsDecisions.title: Tunneling current observed in electric bubbles
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 涉及凝聚态/材料相关关键词，但尚未确证直接实验生长或目标物性的新证据；保留候补，不能仅据标题称已排除。
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: Electric bubbles are sub-10-nm spherical ferroelectric domains promising intriguing functional properties suitable for the next-generation solid-state electronic devices. However, the understanding of their dynamic conductivities, a paramount factor in their circuit integration, remains limited. Here we investigate conduction properties of ferroelectric bubbles using a combination of scanning probe microscopy and first-principles-based simulations. Our experiments reveal that the bubbles exhibit rectifying current-voltage characteristics with ultrahigh direct current densities, attributed to tunneling. Under external electric field, conductivity is maintained or enhanced as long as the original bubble configuration remains stable. On the other hand, when the dipolar configuration is fully disrupted by mechanical force, the conductivity of mechanically switched downward domains decreases by 50%. Our simulations reveal the role of inhomogeneous depolarizing fields and screening conditions which allows for dynamical tuning of the tunneling transport. This ability to control conductivity in ferroelectric bubbles through external stimuli opens new possibilities for their application in future electronic and functional devices.

apsDecisions.title: Single-crystal growth and physical properties of the antiferromagnetic double perovskite Ba 2 CoMoO 6
apsDecisions.readingState: 正式正文和SI精读，具体图表见reading
apsDecisions.selectionReason: 本期已读正式正文、Methods和官方SI
apsDecisions.abstractRawHtml: This work presents a comprehensive investigation of the structural, magnetic, and electronic properties of the double perovskite Ba2CoMoO6 (BCMO). Single crystals were grown via floating-zone and Czochralski growth techniques and characterized using a set of complementary methods. X-ray diffraction analysis confirmed that BCMO crystallizes in a face-centered-cubic (fcc) structure with space group Fm-3m. Magnetic susceptibility measurements exhibit antiferromagnetic ordering below TN=20.1(1) K. A spin-flop transition is observed at 26.5 kOe. Heat capacity measurements and entropy analysis are consistent with a Jeff=1/2 ground state for Co2+ ions. X-ray absorption spectroscopy provided insight into the local electronic structure, revealing the spin-orbit and crystal-field effects. The cluster-model analysis yields a g factor of 4.36, consistent with a spin-orbit-entangled ground state. Surface photovoltage spectroscopy demonstrates a strong near-surface optical response with an onset near 1.5 eV and a pronounced feature at 2.65 eV, consistent with visible-range Co-O-Mo transitions in line with related Ba-based double perovskites, highlighting its potential for spintronic and energy-conversion applications.
